postings.location: Central - United States; West Coast - United States
postings.description:
GAQ227R127

Databricks is seeking an experienced, highly strategic leader to serve as Director of Order to Revenue Compliance. As Databricks continues to scale, protecting our usage-based revenue engine requires dedicated fiduciary oversight at the intersection of product metering, billing systems, and financial accounting. In this key player/coach leadership role, you will lead a specialized team bridging the gap between raw product metering and financial ground truth. You will oversee usage execution, establish product launch controls, direct partner royalty reconciliations, oversee compliance with partnership arrangements, and serve as the primary compliance lead for usage-related SOX controls and audits.

Primary Responsibilities

- Strategic Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and scale a high-performing team consisting of two functional leads covering Partnerships / Royalty, Money/Engineering Compliance, and Issue Resolution. Actively uphold our culture principles and leadership essentials in daily execution.

- Usage & Revenue Fiduciary Oversight: Serve as the primary business and compliance oversight body responsible for ensuring all usage-related, financially impacting processes are accurate, complete, SOX-compliant, and validated prior to customer billing and revenue conversion.

- Partner Agreement & Royalty Governance: Assume complete ownership of outbound/inbound royalty reporting, executions, and complex reconciliations (e.g., Azure/Microsoft, AWS, GCP, SAP). Eliminate manual operational risks, ingestion lag, timing mismatches, and contract-period attribution issues.

- Cross-Functional System Controls & "Two-in-the-Box" Execution: Partner closely with Engineering (Money Team) and Finance Data Systems (FDS) prior to product launches to validate metering, pricing models, SKU additions, and billing logic against business intent.

- Audit Ownership & Technical Accounting: Act as the primary audit lead for external audit, internal audit, and executive stakeholders regarding platform consumption calculations and monetization structures. 

- Remediation & Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Oversee the categorization and resolution of usage issues (Types 1–3), standardize refund SLAs/credits, and drive mandatory cross-functional RCAs with Engineering to prevent systemic metering bugs.

Minimum Qualifications

- Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related technical field; CPA license preferred.

- Experience: 12+ years of relevant experience, including extensive experience in revenue accounting, IT audit, and SOX control frameworks.

- Domain Expertise: Familiarity with ASC 606, specifically applied to consumption-based/usage-based revenue models, SaaS, and complex partner royalty agreements.

- Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence: Proven track record of managing managers or functional leads while directly collaborating with executive leadership across Engineering, Sales Operations, FP&A, and external auditors.

- Technical & Analytical Acumen: Ability to bridge technical systems (product metering engines, SQL/data pipelines, sub-ledgers) with accounting rules and complex contract terms.

postings.title: Director, Revenue Assurance & Ireland Country Lead
postings.description:
GAQ427R220

Mission

Databricks is seeking a senior finance leader based in Ireland to fulfill a dual-impact role: leading our global technical Revenue Assurance function supporting EMEA/APAC regions and serving as the foundational Country Lead for the newly established Databricks Ireland entity.

This high-visibility role combines strategic technical accounting with operational leadership. You will manage a global revenue assurance team while personally establishing and executing key operational processes for Databricks in Ireland.

You will serve as the core on-the-ground finance lead supporting intercompany execution, local contract fulfillment, and revenue assurance oversight to ensure seamless business operations across Ireland and the European Union.

Impact you will have:

Ireland Entity Leadership & Operational Compliance

- Local Entity Execution: Serve as the primary on-the-ground finance leader in Ireland, executing key intercompany agreement workflows required for DBRX Ireland operations.

- Contract & Order Oversight: Support local contract execution workflows on behalf of the entity, ensuring all EU customer order forms and cloud services agreements adhere to established commercial and legal guardrails.

- Intercompany & Revenue Operations Support: Oversee local revenue processes, including EU customer contracting, billing workflows, and payment collection oversight, coordinating closely with Global Order-to-Cash (OtC) and Treasury teams to ensure proper fund-remittance to Databricks, Inc. and compliance with intercompany remittance timelines. 

- Functional Governance: Partner with local and global Legal, Tax, and Treasury stakeholders to maintain local operational compliance, supporting VAT/GST processes (owned by Tax) and legal approvals (owned by Legal).

- Local Capability Expansion: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support hiring and onboarding of additional staff in Ireland to build out long-term operational capabilities for the entity.

postings.description:
MKTQ427R50

As the Director of Technical Marketing at Databricks, you will lead and scale the team responsible for explaining Databricks products, and what you can do with them, at scale to technical buyers and practitioners (from data engineers, data scientists, and ML engineers to solutions architects, platform teams, security engineers, and application developers). You will own the strategy and execution of technical content in written and video form, demos, workshops, launch storytelling, and outbound evangelism that drives technical mindshare, consideration, product adoption, and ultimately pipeline. In the era of agentic marketing and AEO/GEO, your team will increasingly produce content designed to educate both humans and agents alike. You will also play an outsized role in programming the technical content for key Databricks events, such as the Data + AI Summit and Data + AI World Tour, among others. Reporting to the SVP of Product & Solutions Marketing, you will manage a team of 6+ Technical Marketing Managers (growing) and serve as the connective tissue between Product, Product Marketing, Field Engineering, and the broader technical community.

This role expands the traditional TMM charter to include a stronger outbound evangelism dimension, becoming a visible, trusted technical voice externally through social media, YouTube, conferences, and the data practitioner ecosystem while continuing to own the core technical content engine that powers Summit, World Tour, workshops, and field enablement.

The impact you will have:

First 6 months:

- Assess the current TMM team's strengths, gaps, and capacity; establish a clear operating model with defined ownership areas (product coverage, content types, GEO) and a quarterly planning cadence.

- Own and deliver the technical content agenda for Data + AI World Tour and/or the next major Tier 1 event, achieving ≥4.5/5.0 average session ratings and measurable pipeline contribution.

- Launch or significantly expand at least 2 new outbound evangelism motions (e.g., a YouTube series architecture, a technical social media cadence, or a creator/influencer engagement program) that grow Databricks' external technical reach by ≥25%.

- Build an AI-powered publishing engine that enables the TMM team to scale content faster, leveraging AI assistance for content creation and publishing.

- Establish yourself as a credible external technical voice, publishing 3+ original technical pieces (blogs, videos, or talks) and representing Databricks at 2+ external events or podcasts.

- Scale the TMM team to meet growing demand across an expanding set of technical personas (solutions architects, platform engineers, security teams, data scientists, analysts, app developers) driven by the 2026+ product surface (Lakebase, Genie, Lakewatch, Agent Bricks, Omnigent).

- Work with Databricks Field Engineering and FDE (Forward-Deployed Engineering) to capture repeatable product use cases into a Solutions Library, building a motion to scale capture and marketing of these use cases for learning across the entire community.

- Build and operationalize a "1 launch → many assets" content engine that converts every major product launch into persona-specific learning journeys (demos, workshops, blogs, videos, social).

- Grow Databricks' YouTube and social technical content reach by 2x, with a series-based content architecture targeting key personas at multiple depth levels.

- Drive measurable contribution to AEO/GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) ensuring Databricks is cited by default in AI answer engines for key buyer questions.

- Establish Databricks as the default place every technical practitioner learns data + AI, measured by YouTube subscriber growth (target: 300K+), technical content engagement, and Free Edition activation rates tied to content.

- Build a formal Databricks Creators program that turns independent creator reach into co-owned, accurate, early-access content across new product areas.

- Develop the TMM team into a recognized center of excellence — with clear career paths, a strong hiring bar, and a reputation as one of the best technical marketing teams in enterprise software.

- 10+ years of experience in technical marketing, developer relations, solutions engineering, field engineering, or a related technical field in enterprise software / SaaS / cloud.

- 3+ years of people management experience, with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining high-performing technical teams.

- Deep technical fluency in data, AI/ML, and cloud platforms, comfortable building demos and engaging credibly with data engineers, data scientists, solutions architects, and other technical practitioners across the data + AI ecosystem.

- Experience owning technical content strategy for major product launches and flagship events (e.g., user conferences, world tours).

postings.description:
FEQ426R758

Databricks is seeking a Field Chief Technology Officer (Field CTO) for the Americas Industries Business Unit to be a senior, customer-facing technology and business transformation thought leader for our most strategic, often global, accounts in regulated industries. This individual contributor role sits at the intersection of data and AI strategy, industry transformation, and executive relationship-building, working closely with C-level leaders to drive multi-year change on the data platform while representing real-world needs back into Databricks.​

Impact you will have: 

- Build and maintain trusted-advisor relationships with C-level executives (CIO, CDO, CTO, CISO, business COs) in large US-based and global accounts, especially in highly regulated industries (financial services, public sector, healthcare, manufacturing).​

- Proactively cultivate a strong social and professional network across customer executives, boards, key industry bodies, and partners, knowing which organizations and forums to engage to open doors with the right stakeholders.​

- Shape executive thinking on modern data and AI architectures, with emphasis on Lakehouse and data platform modernization as the primary lever for long-term Gen AI impact.​

- Lead C-level briefings, strategy sessions, and multi-day workshops that connect business outcomes, regulatory constraints, and operating model change to concrete Databricks-based roadmaps.​

- Serve as a deep technical counterpart in the field, maintaining L200–L300 proficiency across Databricks products and being able to credibly engage architects, data engineers, and data scientists on solution design and trade-offs.​

- Generalize patterns from the field into reusable reference architectures, industry blueprints, and best practices for regulated industries, and share them through blogs, webinars, whitepapers, and conference keynotes.​

- Orchestrate the broader ecosystem (cloud providers, GSIs, consultancies, ISVs) around customer objectives, ensuring Databricks is at the center of multi-year transformation programs rather than isolated projects.​

- Partner with Account Executives, Solutions Architects, Industry Leads, and Product Specialists to drive complex, multi-year sales cycles, securing platform decisions and expansions while influencing ACV and consumption growth.​

- Provide structured, prioritized feedback from strategic customers into Product, Engineering, and Field leadership to influence product roadmap, especially around data, governance, security, and regulated-industry requirements.​

- Mentor senior Field Engineering and industry-focused talent, contributing to a pipeline of principal- and CTO-level leaders and codifying ways of working for complex, regulated accounts.​

What we look for:

- 15+ years of experience spanning enterprise technology and consulting, including leading or advising on multi-year data platform and analytics transformations in large, complex organizations.​

- Significant time spent inside a large enterprise software or cloud company (e.g., Microsoft or similar) in roles that required navigating matrixed organizations and driving change at scale, combined with direct industry exposure rather than a career spent solely in horizontal software.​

- Experience in or with regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, public sector, regulated manufacturing, utilities), with familiarity with regulatory and compliance considerations affecting data and AI platforms.​

- Background that blends:

- Hands-on technology and architecture work on data platforms and analytics.​

- Organizational and operating model change (ways of working, skills, governance).​

- Executive consulting or advisory, ideally seeing transformations through from strategy to multi-year execution, not only strategy decks.​

- Proven ability to operate as a highly credible peer to C-level executives, driving business-outcome-focused conversations while also diving deep into technical details when needed.​

- Strong, proactive networker who is naturally curious about which associations, councils, and forums matter for a given customer set, and who uses those networks to create new executive entry points and opportunities.​

postings.title: Forward Deployed Program Lead
postings.location: New York City, New York; San Francisco, California
postings.description:
FEQ327R430

Forward Deployed Program Lead

About the team

The Office of the Field CCO works with the Chief Marketing and Chief Revenue Officers of Databricks’ largest customers to redesign how their commercial organizations operate. We build a peer community of CMOs and CROs, partner with them on go-to-market transformation programs, and ensure those programs deliver measurable business results. The work cuts across sales, marketing, field engineering, and partner teams, and it runs on the customer’s own data.

About the role

You will help to shape and lead Databricks’ strategy for driving AI transformations with our customers. You will report directly to the Field CCO. 

This is a role with broad scope that will require you to collaborate across the business: you will set how we deliver transformation engagements, select and run our first 10 pilot accounts, and shape the reusable solutions field engineering builds. You will get work done through account teams, field engineering, field marketing, and enablement. 

What you’ll do

Shape the reusable solutions

- Decide, with field engineering, which pilot solutions become reusable skills and agents (for example, an account research agent or a pipeline risk review) so the next 10 accounts can deploy in weeks rather than months.

- Own how the pieces fit together into a coherent offering for a CMO or CRO: which components combine for which workflow, and what the customer needs in place to use them.

- Pressure-test field engineering’s designs against real customer workflows and set the acceptance criteria an asset must meet before it goes to the field.

- Collaborate with our AI FDE team, product team, and FE regional leadership on the solutionization of workflows/companions.

Set the delivery model

- Define how a GTM transformation engagement runs from first executive conversation to production: stages, roles across account, field engineering, and professional services teams, entry and exit criteria, and governance.

- Set the standard for account plans on transformation opportunities and review each plan with the account team before it goes to the customer. A strong plan names the executive sponsor, the two or three workflows in scope (for example, pipeline forecasting or campaign attribution), the data required, and the business result being targeted.

Select and run the pilot program

- Define the selection criteria for the first 10 pilot accounts (executive sponsorship, data readiness, commercial potential, willingness to go public) and finalize the list with sales leadership.

- Program-manage the pilots. Set the operating cadence: weekly working sessions with account teams, monthly customer steering committees, and a quarterly review with the Field CCO.

- Define and track the metrics for each pilot. Measure business outcomes such as forecast accuracy, sales cycle length, or cost per qualified lead, alongside workflow adoption and consumption.

- Identify stalled pilots early and escalate with a specific recovery plan.

Build the CMO and CRO community

- Partner with field marketing to launch and run CMO and CRO councils across North America and EMEA: membership criteria, agenda, and a format that gives members a reason to return.

- Partner with the Office of the CMO on thought leadership for flagship events such as Data + AI Summit and executive dinners, including keynote narratives, customer case studies drawn from the pilots, and point-of-view papers on how commercial organizations are changing.

Enable the field

- Partner with ops and the enablement team to build the mechanisms that teach field engineers and sellers how the solutions work, when to position them, and how to deploy them: playbooks, demo environments, certification paths, and deal reviews.

Minimum Qualifications

- Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, or equivalent professional experience.

- Experience: 5-7+ years in product development of highly technical products, product operations, GTM strategy, business operations, technical program management, or deploying technical/AI solutions with customers.

- Cross-Organizational Execution: 4+ years collaborating on cross-functional programs that drive committed outcomes across Product, Field Engineering, and Marketing, including at the executive level.

- Communication: Ability to communicate technical concepts to both non-technical and technically proficient audiences, including tailoring messages for potential customers and executives.

- AI & Automation: Demonstrated and creative use of AI-driven tooling and automated workflows.

- Sales/Marketing Expertise: Experience building or working with MarTech/SalesTech, including an understanding of marketing workflows, MMM, MROI, and GTM ontologies. 

Preferred Qualifications

- Hands-On AI Agent Deployment: Direct experience scoping, deploying, or evaluating AI agents or predictive analytics workflows (experience with product development for AI agents a plus).

- Some coding experience with React, TypeScript, SQL, or Go.

- MBA or equivalent professional experience. 

- Experience with customer-facing strategy, GTM strategy, or value engineering at a high-growth data or AI software company (experience interfacing with end customers to influence software development preferred).

postings.title: Global SAP Consolidations Manager
postings.description:
GAQ327R292

We're building a finance function that stays ahead of the curve - leveraging AI, automation, and modern tooling to operate at the pace Databricks demands. We are looking for a Global Consolidations Manager to join our Global Accounting team based in India. This is a foundational hire - you will own the end-to-end consolidation and intercompany accounting process across Databricks' 23-entity global footprint, build deep SAP Group Reporting expertise during our S/4HANA implementation, and establish the permanent organisational capability that scales with the business post go-live.

This role blends hands-on consolidation execution with technical accounting judgment. As part of the Global Accounting organisation, you will ensure the accurate and timely production of consolidated financial statements under both US GAAP and IFRS, while partnering closely with International Accounting, Corporate Accounting, Tax, and FP&A to drive close integrity across all reporting frameworks.

The impact you will have: 

- Own and execute the global consolidation process end-to-end - intercompany reconciliation, elimination entries, currency translation, and multi-entity roll-up across our 23-entity footprint.

- Lead multi-GAAP close execution, producing parallel US GAAP and IFRS consolidated books each period, identifying and documenting reconciling differences for audit and leadership review.

- Build and own SAP Group Reporting expertise - serve as the accounting team's subject matter expert on SAP's consolidation engine, including configuration, period-end processing, and ongoing optimisation.

- Execute intercompany accounting across all entities - ensuring balances are reconciled, disputes are resolved within the close window, and elimination entries are complete and accurate.

- Perform monthly consolidation flux analysis, identifying and clearly articulating drivers behind significant period-over-period movements for leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Own FX translation and revaluation accounting - functional currency determination, translation adjustments, and CTA reconciliation across all international entities.

- Support new entity stand-up - partner with Tax, Legal, and International Accounting to establish consolidation processes, intercompany agreements, and reporting structures for new international selling entities as Databricks expands.

- Serve as a primary point of contact for internal and external audit on consolidation, intercompany, and multi-GAAP reporting matters. Champion compliance with SOX controls across the consolidation process.

- Drive AI and automation adoption across consolidation workflows - including automated intercompany matching, elimination entry generation, and reconciliation tooling leveraging the Databricks platform.

- Partner with the Senior Manager, Close & Consolidation (US) to ensure seamless handoff and time-zone coverage for the most time-sensitive part of the global close.

What we look for:

- BA/BS Degree with a focus in Economics, Business Administration, Accounting, or Finance.

- 10+ years progressive accounting experience, with at least 5+ years specifically in consolidation, intercompany accounting, or international accounting within a US multinational framework.

- A Chartered Accountant (CA) or CPA equivalent certification is mandatory. 

- Deep understanding of US GAAP consolidation requirements (ASC 810, ASC 830) and working knowledge of IFRS consolidation standards (IFRS 10, IAS 21). Multi-GAAP reporting experience is strongly preferred.

- SAP S/4HANA experience required - specifically SAP Group Reporting or SAP BPC. Candidates with implementation experience will be prioritized.

- Proven experience managing intercompany accounting at scale - reconciliation, netting, dispute resolution, and elimination across a multi-entity, multi-currency environment.

- Experience with FX translation, functional currency assessment, and CTA accounting across complex international structures.

- Proven track record driving automation and process improvement in consolidation or close operations.

- Experience supporting external audits and SOX compliance in a consolidation context.

- Proven experience partnering with remote teams across different geographic areas, including with US-based accounting leadership, and the flexibility to support close timelines that span US Pacific Time hours.

postings.title: GTM Strategy Manager
postings.location: Remote - California; San Francisco, California; USCA
postings.description:
SLSQ227R805

While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations will be considered.
Candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role

- San Francisco

The Partner Strategy team works directly with Databricks' Partnerships leaders to drive operational scale across our Consulting and Systems Integrator ecosystem, in an extremely high-growth environment. We give our stakeholders and senior leadership the insights, tools, and decision criteria to shape proactive, effective, data-driven programmatic strategies.

We're looking for a Strategy Manager to be the business partner to the VP of Global Systems Integrators. It's a critical, high-visibility role built on two elements:

- Strategic business partner to GSI leadership. You partner with the VP of Global Systems Integrators to set the strategy and medium- to long-term goals for the business. Then you lead the execution: building scalable processes, building consensus, and running programs end to end. You're the connective tissue across Partnerships, Sales, Product, Finance, Data, Legal, Commercial, and the broader GTM org. You invest the time to know the SI landscape, our GSI partners, and the SI operating model.

- A highly technical, analytical operator. You love working with data. You're AI-fluent, and you use cutting-edge AI and data tools for analysis, problem solving, visualization, and automation. You'll own the executive analyses and deep dives that turn SI performance trends into action.

You must be able to run the day-to-day operating cadence with rigor, while also stepping back to bring a strategic point of view the leader hasn't asked for yet. You will report to the Director of Partner Strategy & Operations.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape and scale the strategy behind one of Databricks' most important growth engines: our Global Systems Integrator partnerships.

The impact you'll have

- Be the strategic business partner to the VP of Global Systems Integrators. Know the GSI partners, programs, and numbers well enough to surface risks, opportunities, and recommendations before you're asked.

- Own the operating cadence for the GSI business. Run the rhythm of the business and give clear visibility into performance against targets.

- Lead executive analyses and deliverables, such as board materials and QBRs, with a point of view, not just data.

- Define and run high-impact cross-functional programs end to end, from strategy through execution.

- Turn data and voice of the field into a better SI strategy. Dig into GSI performance trends and drive them to action that improves SI strategy and programs.

- Guide annual GTM planning for the GSI business: FY and long-range modeling, KPI setting, and HC planning.

What we look for

- Relevant experience. 7+ years of strategy & operations experience (e.g., Enterprise SaaS, top-tier strategy consulting, investment banking, business operations).

- Business ownership. You have the leadership and confidence to partner with VP-level GTM stakeholders like you own the business, not support them from the sidelines.

- Relentless problem solving. You love to analyze, set priorities, and solve complex problems. You dig deeper to find root causes, and you're not afraid to ask questions.

- AI and technical fluency. AI and data tools are part of your daily workflow for analysis, problem solving, data visualization, and automation. You keep learning and growing your skills, and you know the common GTM tech stack (Databricks, SFDC, Tableau, SQL, etc.).

- Comfort with ambiguity. Our GSI business is growing fast in scope and complexity, so things won't always be clean or easy. You embrace that challenge and are excited to build for scale.

- SI ecosystem fluency. You understand the Systems Integrator, GTM, or sales/partner operating model, and you have the judgment to weigh tradeoffs within it.

What this role isn't

- Not an order-taker or reporting function. You're expected to partner with the VP of Global Systems Integrators to set strategy and own outcomes, not wait for tasks to be assigned.

- Not a pure strategy role. You'll lead execution of the initiatives you help define. Building processes and consensus is part of the job, not optional.

- Not a static environment. The GSI business keeps expanding in scope and complexity. If you prefer clean, well-defined problems, this isn't the right fit.

postings.description:
MKTQ127R2

Databricks is seeking an exceptional marketing leader to serve as Head of Marketing for Japan. As Head of Marketing for Japan, you will serve as the country marketing leader and strategic business partner to the Japan leadership team helping shape overall go-to-market strategy.

You will be responsible for defining and executing Databricks’ integrated marketing strategy for Japan to accelerate category leadership, pipeline growth, customer adoption, and long-term market expansion. This includes building Databricks’ reputation and presence in one of our most strategic global markets while ensuring marketing is deeply aligned to business priorities across sales, partners, customer success, and corporate functions.

This role requires a highly strategic, commercially-minded marketing executive who can balance long-term market development with near-term revenue accountability.

Reporting to the VP Marketing, APJ, you will lead cross-functional orchestration across global, APJ, and in-country teams to deliver high-impact, locally relevant programs that drive measurable business outcomes.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Business & Market Leadership

- Serve as the senior marketing leader and trusted advisor to the Japan leadership team, contributing to country strategy and operating as a key voice in market planning and execution.

- Own country marketing strategy across reputation, demand, customer engagement, and ecosystem development.

- Partner closely with country sales leadership to align marketing investments with strategic growth priorities, whitespace opportunities, and account segmentation.

Integrated Marketing Strategy

- Develop and execute Japan’s end-to-end marketing strategy across brand, demand generation, executive engagement, customer marketing, communications, and events.

- Ensure global and APJ campaigns are effectively localized and activated to maximize impact in-market.

- Build innovative, high-performing programs tailored to Japan’s unique buyer, cultural, and market dynamics.

Partner Marketing & Ecosystem Development

- Develop partner marketing strategy in close partnership with alliances and cloud ecosystem teams.

- Leverage partners as a force multiplier to expand market reach, accelerate pipeline creation, and deepen customer engagement.

- Build joint go-to-market motions with strategic ecosystem partners.

AI-First Marketing Leadership

- Champion modern, AI-enabled marketing practices and help evolve the Japan marketing organization toward AI-native ways of working.

- Demonstrate fluency in emerging AI technologies and their implications for marketing execution, productivity, and customer engagement.

- Continuously identify opportunities to improve marketing effectiveness through data, automation, and AI.

Team Leadership & Talent Development

- Coach and mentor talent to elevate strategic thinking, executional excellence, and future leadership capability.

- Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Success Measures / Outcomes

- Drive measurable contribution to pipeline, consumption, and customer adoption targets in Japan.

- Increase Databricks’ reputation, awareness, and category leadership.

- Expand partner-sourced / partner-influenced pipeline contribution.

- Build a high-performing, scalable marketing team and operating model for Japan.

- Establish marketing as a strategic growth driver and trusted business partner to the Japan leadership team.

What We Look For

- 15+ years of progressive marketing leadership experience in enterprise technology / high-growth software environments.

- Proven experience leading country or regional marketing organizations in Japan.

- Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic business leader and partner to senior sales / country executives.

- Strong experience across field marketing, demand generation, executive engagement, partner marketing, communications, and events.

- Deep understanding of enterprise go-to-market models and complex B2B buying journeys.

- Strong commercial acumen with fluency in pipeline, funnel, and revenue metrics.

- Demonstrated experience building and developing high-performing teams.

- Strong understanding of AI’s impact on marketing and go-to-market, with ability to lead modern AI-enabled marketing transformation.

- Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills.

- Native / fluent Japanese and business-level English required.

postings.title: Incident Manager
postings.description:
Incident Manager

US Remote

CSQ127R151

At Databricks, we are passionate about empowering data teams to tackle the world’s most challenging problems — from bringing the next mode of transportation to reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We achieve this by building and operating the world’s best data and AI infrastructure platform, enabling our customers to leverage deep data insights and enhance their business. Founded by engineers — and customer-obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to tackle technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

As an Incident Manager, you will lead Databricks’ most critical production incidents while providing clear, accurate, and timely communication to customers, executives, and engineers. You’ll serve as both incident commander and reliability engineer; orchestrating multi-team responses, driving real-time status updates, and partnering with engineering to analyze and prevent failures. Your work will ensure Databricks maintains not only technical resilience but also customer and stakeholder confidence during high-impact events.

This role combines operational leadership, technical systems knowledge, and exceptional communication skills. You will be at the intersection of engineering depth and operational clarity, ensuring that every major incident is managed with precision, transparency, and continuous improvement.

- Lead critical incidents — coordinate multi-disciplinary response efforts across Databricks’ cloud-based services to rapidly mitigate impact and restore operations.

- Drive technical root cause analysis and reliability improvements:

- collaborate with engineering teams to trace and document underlying causes across distributed systems, services, and data stores.

- Summarize key learnings, clearly communicate action items, and ensure that technical and procedural improvements are followed through.

- Own communications during incidents — deliver frequent, high-quality updates to internal stakeholders (executives, engineering leadership, support) and compose and publish customer-facing notifications that are accurate, timely, and empathetic.

- Familiarity with log aggregation and search tools (e.g., Datadog, Elasticsearch, Splunk, Cloud Logging, or OpenTelemetry).

- Hands-on experience with observability systems — metrics, logging, and tracing frameworks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, etc.).

- Proficiency in at least one major programming or scripting language (Python, Go, or Bash) for automating diagnostics, data collection, or analysis.

- Experience developing and maintaining incident playbooks and communication templates to ensure consistent, timely updates.

- Excellent contextual interpretation and writing skills, as well as the ability to effectively summarize and communicate to both technical and business audiences, are required.

postings.description:
SLSQ327R321

While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations will be considered.

Databricks is seeking a Lakebase Associate Director to help customers modernize their operational data foundation with Databricks Lakebase, our fully-managed Postgres offering for intelligent applications. This high-impact role sits within the Lakebase Go-To-Market team and partners closely with Industry Account Executives within our Financial Services vertical to drive adoption of Lakebase with platform, application, and data teams.

Lakebase gives customers a unified, governed foundation for operational workloads and AI-native applications, helping them move away from a fragmented estate of point databases toward a modern, scalable, serverless Postgres service. If you want to be at the forefront of operational databases for AI and intelligent applications at one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world, this is your opportunity.

The impact you will have

- Drive new Lakebase revenue by identifying, qualifying, and driving Lakebase activations and consumption within a defined territory, in partnership with regional Account Executives and the broader account team.

- Lead with outcomes for key Lakebase personas — including platform teams and developers, data teams, and central IT — articulating how Lakebase helps them ship features faster, simplify operational data architectures, and improve governance and cost efficiency.

- Sell the value of fully-managed Postgres for intelligent applications, positioning Lakebase as the optimal choice for operational workloads that power real-time, AI-driven experiences.

- Run complex, multi-threaded sales cycles from discovery and value hypothesis through commercial negotiation and close, navigating executive, technical, and line-of-business stakeholders.

- Orchestrate proof-of-value and POCs that validate Lakebase’s benefits for OLTP-style workloads, reverse ETL, and AI/ML-driven applications, in partnership with solution architects and specialists.

- Compete and win against legacy and cloud-native operational databases by leveraging our compete assets, benchmarks, and customer references.

- Align to measurable business outcomes such as performance, developer productivity, time-to-market for new features, cost reduction, and simplification of the operational data landscape.

- Partner cross-functionally with Product Management, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partner teams to shape territory plans, launch plays, and co-selling motions with key ISVs and GSIs.

- Enable the field by sharing Lakebase best practices, success stories, and sales motions with broader sales teams, helping scale Lakebase proficiency across the organization.

What success looks like in this role

This role requires the ability to operate across two key motions simultaneously:

- Establish top strategic focus accounts by engaging application development teams to create net-new intelligent applications leveraging Lakebase.

- Drive longer-term Postgres standardization and migration within Databricks' most strategic accounts.

Candidates should demonstrate how they can act as a force multiplier across multiple dimensions of the business.

Success in this role requires strength in four areas:

- Business ownership – Operate at a business-unit level by tracking revenue, pipeline, and key observations, and by identifying areas needing additional focus or support.

- Strategic account engagement – Partner with account teams to engage priority accounts across the global DB700, driving strategic opportunities from initial engagement through successful outcomes.

- Field, account, & customer enablement: Align customers and the field on the value of Lakebase by equipping AEs and SAs with the messaging and execution motions needed to confidently own accounts without specialist intervention.

- Market voice and thought leadership – Develop an internal and external presence by contributing to global AMAs and internal forums, and by representing Databricks at key first- and third-party events.

The interview process is designed to evaluate candidates across all four of these dimensions.

What we look for

- 7+ years of enterprise SaaS sales experience, consistently exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder deals.

- Proven success selling data platforms, operational databases (e.g., Postgres, MySQL, cloud-native DBaaS), or adjacent data/AI infrastructure to technical buyers and business leaders.

- Strong understanding of modern data and application architectures, including cloud-native services, microservices, event-driven systems, and how operational data underpins AI and analytics strategies.

- Ability to sell to both technical stakeholders (developers, architects, data engineers) and business stakeholders (product leaders, operations, line-of-business owners).

- Demonstrated experience leading specialist or overlay motions, working jointly with core Account Executives to create and progress opportunities.

- Executive presence with the ability to whiteboard architectures, lead C-level conversations, and build trust with senior decision makers.

- Strong value selling skills: adept at discovering pain, building a business case, and tying technical capabilities to clear, quantified outcomes.

- Excellent communication, storytelling, and negotiation skills, with comfort presenting to both large and small audiences.

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience selling Postgres, operational databases, OLTP workloads, or transactional cloud database services, ideally within large or strategic accounts.

- Familiarity with data platforms, Lakehouse architectures, and cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP), including how operational databases fit within broader data and AI strategies.

- Understanding of reverse ETL, real-time decisioning, and operational analytics use cases, and how they drive value for customer-facing and internal applications.

- Exposure to AI-native and agent-driven applications that depend on low-latency, highly scalable operational data services.

- Prior experience in a high-growth, category-creating environment, helping shape new plays, messaging, and customer narratives.

- Experience collaborating with partners and ISVs to drive joint pipeline and co-sell motions.

Pay Range Transparency

Databricks is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The pay range(s) for this role is listed below and represents the expected salary range for non-commissionable roles or on-target earnings for commissionable roles. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, relevant certifications and training, and specific work location. Databricks is looking for a talented and experienced Lead Counsel to support strategic technology partnerships and other specialty initiatives. You will report to the VP & Associate General Counsel, Strategic Alliances & Integration 

Strategic partnerships are an essential pillar to Databricks' providing the world's leading data & AI platform, integrating the broadest range of the latest leading technologies from proven partner providers. In this role, you will work closely with Databricks Strategic Alliances and cross-functional stakeholders, orchestrating advice and contributions across internal and external experts, and innovating to provide solutions in a rapidly evolving landscape. 

A successful candidate will have deep proven experience navigating and negotiating complex, highly operational agreements with technology partners, including leading AI Model Providers and global hyperscalers, working with a wide range of internal stakeholders at all levels, including regular direct engagement with senior leadership. You must be an agile, resourceful self-starter, comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, and excellent at building strong relationships and giving clear, pragmatic advice. You have a bias for action, enjoy building, thrive on finding creative solutions to new challenges, and value seeing your direct impact on the business. 

The impact you will have:

- Lead and manage all legal aspects of selected Strategic Alliance technology transactions, including term sheet negotiations, running deal processes and negotiations, reviewing, drafting, and negotiating documents, securing and coordinating engagement and contributions from cross-functional stakeholders, including Product, Finance, Security, Procurement, Commercial Legal, Product Legal, GTM Legal, and other internal and external experts

- You have at least 10 years of experience at a nationally recognized law firm and / or in-house legal department at a high-tech company

postings.title: Lead Solutions Architect - Generative AI (EMEA Emerging DNB)
postings.description:
REQ ID: FEQ227R147

Location: United Kingdom (Remote/Hybrid — London or UK-based)

Recruiter: Dina Hussain

About the Role

We are looking for a Lead Solution Architect focused on Generative AI to support our EMEA Emerging Digital Natives and Startups business unit — one of the fastest-moving, most technically ambitious patches in EMEA. Our customers are digital-native and cloud-native companies who build on the frontier: they adopt GenAI early, scale fast, and expect their technical partners to be as sharp as their own engineers.

You will be the go-to expert our Account Teams and customers turn to when a GenAI or LLM use case needs to move from an ambitious idea to a production-grade reality across our high-growth accounts.

This is a highly technical, customer-facing individual contributor role for someone who lives at the frontier of applied GenAI. You will shape architectures, prove out the hard problems, challenge and influence customer roadmaps, and raise the GenAI capability of the entire EMEA Emerging DNB field organisation.

What You'll Do

- Serve as the deep technical authority on Generative AI, LLMs, and applied machine learning for the EMEA Emerging DNB business unit, supporting the most strategic and complex customer engagements across our digital-native and born-in-the-cloud accounts.

- Partner with our EMEA Emerging DNB Solutions Architects, Solutions Engineers, and Account teams to scope, design, and de-risk GenAI use cases — from retrieval-augmented generation and agentic systems to fine-tuning and evaluation.

- Build hands-on proofs of concept and reference implementations that operationalise large-scale LLM and deep learning workloads on Databricks (Mosaic AI, MLflow, Model Serving, Vector Search, Unity Catalog governance), tuned to the fast iteration cycles Emerging DNB customers expect.

- Lead fine-tuning and model-customisation engagements on open LLMs (e.g., Llama-family models), including judge-based and label-efficient evaluation approaches for domains where quality and safety are paramount.

- Act as a bridge to Product and Engineering — channel field and customer feedback into the roadmap and represent the roadmap back to the field.

- Enable and mentor the broader EMEA Emerging DNB Field Engineering team through workshops, reference architectures, and internal enablement, multiplying GenAI expertise across our ~70-person SA/SE organisation.

- Represent Databricks externally as a technical thought leader — conference talks (e.g., Data + AI Summit), blogs, and customer executive briefings.

What We're Looking For

- Strong understanding of the LLM landscape, including leading proprietary and open-source models and providers, with the ability to differentiate their capabilities, trade-offs, and suitability for different use cases, and to articulate a clear, informed point of view (POV) to customers.

- Deep expertise in the modern GenAI stack: LLM application patterns (RAG, agents, tool use), fine-tuning and model customization, prompt and evaluation engineering, and LLM guardrails/safety.

- Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, including distributed training, GPU workloads, and the full MLOps lifecycle (tracking, registry, serving, monitoring).

- Proficiency in Python and the ML ecosystem (PyTorch/Transformers, MLflow, Spark), and comfort building production-quality reference implementations.

- Experience with the Databricks platform — or the ability to ramp on it quickly — including Mosaic AI, Model Serving, Vector Search, and Unity Catalog. Cloud experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.

- Excellent communication and consultative skills: able to earn the trust of both hands-on engineers and senior technical executives, and to explain complex GenAI trade-offs clearly.

- A track record of technical leadership and mentorship — someone who elevates the people around them.

- Comfort operating at the pace of digital-native and high-growth customers, where speed, iteration, and technical credibility win the deal.

- Based in the United Kingdom and able to work across EMEA time zones, with willingness to travel to customer sites within the region as needed.

- Background helping digital-native customers build data and ML solutions (e.g., prior experience at a data/ML platform or consulting vendor) is a strong plus.

Nice to Have

- Public technical presence: conference speaking, published talks, blogs, or open-source contributions in the ML/GenAI space.

- Domain depth in a regulated or high-stakes industry (healthcare/life sciences, financial services) where model quality, evaluation, and safety are critical.

- Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to influence roadmap.

Why This Role

You will work on the hardest and most exciting GenAI problems our EMEA Emerging DNB customers have — companies building the future in real time — with the platform and the people to actually solve them, not just advise. You'll shape how one of EMEA's highest-growth business units adopts Generative AI, influence the direction of the product, and build a public profile as a recognised expert in the field. This is the role for a builder and a teacher, who wants their expertise to have outsized impact.

About Databricks

More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. postings.description:
(FEQ128R42)

The Role

You will be the technical leader and lead architect for one of Databricks' most strategic global customers: a health technology company whose diagnostic, therapy, connected-care and consumer health products reach hundreds of millions of people every year. You will own the technical relationship and the Data + AI vision for a single complex enterprise that spans multiple business units, regions and regulatory regimes.

The account is a large, Azure-first Data Intelligence Platform customer. It runs a portfolio of well over a hundred use cases across business units and global functions, delivered as a multi-year program in quarterly releases. You will set the technical direction for that program and turn it into an executable roadmap. You will work as one team with the Account Executive and a dedicated pod of Solutions Architects, specialists, Professional Services and partners. We are looking for a visionary who can see where Data + AI will take health technology, explain that clearly to executives and engineers alike, and bring a large, distributed group of people with them!

The Impact You Will Have

Own and drive the technical vision

- Define the customer's enterprise Data + AI vision with CxO and VP stakeholders, tied directly to business priorities. Be the executive suite's trusted advisor on platform strategy, build-vs-buy, responsible AI and regulated-industry governance.

- Show, don't tell: inspire CTOs, chief architects and engineering leaders with working examples, and build prototypes yourself when it matters.

- Lead the account pod technically: set direction for Solutions Architects, Specialist and Delivery SAs, Professional Services and partners, and coach them to raise the bar.

- Partner with the Account Executive on account strategy and consumption planning, owning technical strategy and path to value for every major initiative.

- Align pre-sales, delivery and partners so the customer sees one Databricks team, one plan and one escalation path, local to global. Lead discovery and solution design for strategic, high-risk deployments, driving each to production and measurable outcomes.

- Build lasting C-level, VP and Director relationships across IT, data & AI, R&D, Quality & Regulatory, Service, Operations and the business units.

- Be the customer's voice internally, shaping Databricks product and go-to-market strategy with field insight while leading the account's largest modernisation programs

- Scale GenAI and agentic AI from pilot to production across business units.

- Build partner ecosystem relationships (GSIs, ISVs, hyperscalers) to scale delivery.

- Create reusable IP (reference designs, accelerators, talks, blogs) for the wider Databricks health and life sciences community.

What We Look For

(Note: it is not expected that you “tick every box” below and encourage you to apply if you are meeting several of the key criteria and can demonstrate a strong ability to transfer skills and develop quickly in the role!) 

- Proven record as lead technical figure on a large global enterprise account, or as enterprise/chief architect at a similar organisation, owning the vision over multiple years.

- Experience leading virtual teams without direct authority: setting direction, coaching senior architects and aligning specialists, delivery and partners on one plan.

- Thrives with high autonomy in ambiguous, high-stakes, multi-region, multi-business-unit environments. Excellent communicator, from boardroom to engineering floor, with clear written thinking.

Technical depth

- 10+ years in data engineering, analytics, ML or AI architecture, with significant customer-facing technical leadership (pre-sales, consulting or enterprise architecture).

- Deep, hands-on expertise in modern data and AI platforms; Apache Spark, Delta Lake and Databricks experience is a strong plus.

- Experience designing:

- Large-scale data platforms and migrations from legacy warehouses, Hadoop or other clouds

- Enterprise governance and security models

- Production ML, MLOps, GenAI and agent systems

- Proven ability to win platform decisions against hyperscaler-native and competing platforms on architecture, cost and governance.

- Proficient in Python and SQL; able to prototype quickly, including with AI-assisted development.

Domain knowledge

- Experience in health technology, medical devices, life sciences or another regulated industry, and a passion for improving patient outcomes with Data + AI.

- Understanding of privacy and data-sharing regimes (GDPR, HIPAA, European Health Data Space). Familiarity with healthcare data standards (DICOM, HL7, FHIR, OMOP).

Nice to Have

- Familiarity working in or with MedTech and medical AI regulation, with examples such as: EU MDR/IVDR, FDA SaMD, ISO 13485, IEC 62304, ISO 14971

- Experience designing validated, audit-ready (GxP / 21 CFR Part 11) data and AI environments. Enterprise-scale SAP data integration (BW, S/4HANA) and semantic harmonisation.

- Public thought leadership: conference talks, publications or open source.

- Dutch is a plus; professional English required.

postings.title: Lead Technical Enablement Specialist, Field Capability & Readiness
postings.description:
SLSQ227R703

About the Role

The Field Engineering role is changing quickly. AI is changing how technical work gets done, products and customer needs are evolving faster, and the capabilities that distinguish an exceptional FE today will not be exactly the same ones that matter tomorrow.

Databricks is looking for a Lead Technical Enablement Specialist to help define and build the capability engine for our global Field Engineering organization. You will shape how FEs build expertise, demonstrate readiness, share what they know, and apply their capabilities with customers.

This role owns a portfolio, not a single program. That portfolio may include skills verification, technical validation, role-based readiness paths, practical challenges, and new approaches we have not yet imagined. Your job is to understand where the field is headed, identify the capabilities that will matter most, and turn that insight into experiences and systems that help FEs grow and perform.

This is a high-visibility, high-autonomy role for someone who wants to build. You will work with FE leaders, product and technical communities, regional teams, enablement partners, HR, and internal platform teams to define what “field-ready” means and make it useful in the flow of work. You will have the opportunity to influence how a global technical organization develops - and to create programs that become part of how Databricks operates.

The best person for this role is equal parts strategist, product thinker, builder, and operator. You can see around corners, create structure from ambiguity, earn trust with senior stakeholders, and turn an idea into something the field actually uses. You are energized by the possibility of using AI not only as a topic to teach, but as a catalyst to redesign how capability is built, measured, and scaled.

What You'll Do

- Set the vision and roadmap for FE capability. Develop a clear point of view on how Databricks should build, demonstrate, recognize, and continuously evolve field expertise. Translate FE strategy, product priorities, customer needs, and the changing nature of technical work into a focused portfolio of investments.

- Own and evolve a portfolio of readiness experiences. Bring together existing programs and new opportunities across skills verification, technical demonstrations, role-based pathways, credentials, and practical application. Decide what to scale, redesign, connect, or retire to keep the portfolio coherent and valuable.

- Invent new ways for FEs to build and prove expertise. When the field needs a new capability, design the right experience - not automatically another course. This could be a customer scenario, a live technical demonstration, a peer review, a contribution model, an AI-enabled assessment, or something entirely new. Prototype quickly, learn from the field, and scale the strongest ideas.

- Make readiness relevant to the work FEs actually do. Partner with practitioners, managers, product teams, and SME communities to define credible standards and evidence of capability. Embed development and validation into existing FE workflows wherever possible, making readiness a pull-based experience rather than an additional layer of process.

- Help the organization adapt to an AI-enabled future. Stay close to how AI is changing FE workflows, technical depth, customer engagement, and delivery models. Ensure our capability models measure judgment, problem-solving, architecture, collaboration, and customer impact - not just static product knowledge. Experiment with AI to improve assessment quality, personalize development, surface expertise, and scale program operations responsibly.

- Create the systems and signals that make capability visible. Partner with internal platform and engineering teams to turn program concepts into simple, scalable experiences. Ensure that skills, evidence, readiness milestones, and development recommendations are useful to FEs, managers, and leaders in the systems they already use.

- Build the operating model for a federated technical organization. Establish clear ownership, governance, quality standards, content and assessment lifecycles, and feedback loops across global programs, product SMEs, regional leaders, and enablement partners. Create mechanisms that let expertise scale without centralizing every decision.

- Drive adoption through influence and strong field experience. Build the narrative, stakeholder plan, manager engagement, and operating rhythm needed to make programs matter. Listen carefully to the field, remove friction, and use adoption data and qualitative feedback to improve the experience.

- Give leaders a clear view of capability and opportunity. Define meaningful measures of participation, proficiency, capability coverage, readiness, and emerging gaps. Use data to help leaders decide where to invest, where to raise the bar, and how the FE organization is evolving.

- Connect capability to growth and career opportunities. Partner with FE leadership, HR, and career architecture owners to make demonstrated capability useful in development conversations, specialization paths, succession planning, and career progression where appropriate.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

- Established a compelling, shared point of view on what FE capability and readiness need to look like in an AI-enabled Databricks.

- Created a clear roadmap for the field capability portfolio, with explicit priorities and decisions about what to scale, improve, or stop.

- Launched or materially evolved high-value readiness experiences that FEs and managers see as relevant to their work - not administrative requirements.

- Built strong partnerships across FE leadership, product and technical communities, regional teams, HR, and internal platform teams.

- Given leaders and managers better visibility into capability, gaps, and trends - and helped them act on those signals.

- Established a scalable operating model that enables expertise to grow across the organization without creating unnecessary central processes.

- Demonstrated measurable progress in adoption, capability coverage, field confidence, or other outcomes that matter to the business.

What We're Looking For

- 6+ years of experience in technical enablement, product management, learning and development, consulting, field engineering, or program leadership within a high-growth technology company.

- A track record of building and scaling something new from ambiguity. You have shaped the strategy, aligned stakeholders, designed the experience, launched it, measured it, and improved it over time.

- Strong strategic judgment and executive presence. You can partner with Directors and VPs to shape priorities, make tradeoffs, challenge assumptions constructively, and turn a broad vision into clear decisions.

- A product mindset. You start with the user and the problem, test assumptions, design for adoption, and continuously improve the experience based on evidence.

- The ability to balance rigor with practicality. You know how to create credible standards and meaningful signals without adding unnecessary friction for the field.

- Strong data fluency. You can define useful measures, interpret dashboards, identify patterns, and use data and field feedback to drive decisions. 

- Experience partnering with internal product, engineering, or platform teams to turn program requirements into scalable tools and workflows.

- Genuine curiosity about AI and its impact on technical work, customer engagement, and organizational capability. Hands-on experience using AI to improve assessment, personalization, content, or operations is a plus.

- Enough technical fluency in data and AI to work credibly with technical experts and evaluate whether readiness standards are relevant and meaningful - or the curiosity and learning agility to build that fluency quickly.

- Excellent communication skills. You can translate between technical practitioners, SME communities, enablement teams, regional leaders, and executive stakeholders.

- A strong ownership mindset, with the pace, creativity, and judgment to operate effectively in a distributed, cross-functional environment.

Nice to Have

- Experience designing skills taxonomies, competency frameworks, technical certifications, assessment models, or role-based capability systems.

- Experience building community-driven models for sharing and validating expertise, such as peer review, SME networks, contribution-based credentials, or practitioner communities.

- Familiarity with learning science, adult learning, assessment design, or evidence-based evaluation.

- Experience integrating capability or enablement programs with internal platforms, such as skills systems, LMS platforms, CRM systems, or custom enterprise tools.

- Experience with industry-specific enablement or vertical go-to-market strategies in enterprise software.

- Experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as solutions architecture, sales engineering, consulting, technical account management, or data and AI engineering.

Why This Role Matters

A global FE organization cannot scale its impact through content and training alone. It needs a shared view of what great looks like, practical ways for people to build and demonstrate expertise, strong communities that spread knowledge, and useful signals that help leaders invest in the right capabilities.

This role will help build that system for Databricks. You will shape how the FE organization responds to the AI era, make expertise more visible and transferable, and create the conditions for thousands of FEs to grow their impact with customers. The work will be visible, highly cross-functional, and consequential to how Field Engineering operates in the future.

United States – Apply Now

As a Delivery Solutions Architect (DSA) Manager supporting our Healthcare & Life Sciences (HLS) segment, you will lead a team of DSAs responsible for accelerating production-grade Data and AI workloads across some of the most regulated, mission-critical environments in the world. Your organization will be the technical engine behind how payers, providers, med-tech, and biopharma customers modernize clinical intelligence, streamline R&D operations, and operationalize secure AI at scale on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform.

You will define strategy, set the execution rhythm, and coach a team capable of navigating long implementation cycles, strict compliance requirements, and multi-stakeholder enterprise programs—all while ensuring customers achieve clear, measurable outcomes. You will report to the Director of Delivery Solutions Architecture for the HLS Business Unit.

Build and Lead a High-Performing HLS Delivery Team

Hire, develop, and inspire DSAs who can navigate clinical, scientific, and operational workloads. Establish a performance culture grounded in accuracy, velocity, and architectural excellence.

Accelerate Production in Highly Regulated Environments

Guide your team to minimize onboarding friction, remove blockers, and bring critical HLS use cases—clinical analytics, real-world evidence, supply-chain intelligence, quality systems, AI/ML—into production quickly and safely.

Drive Compliance-Aware Technical Excellence

postings.title: Manager, Developer Relations - Open Source
postings.description:
RDQ427R541

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's most challenging problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI platform, enabling our customers to use deep data insights to improve their businesses. Our ability to execute this mission depends on building trust and recognition within an ever-growing community of data engineers, analysts, scientists, machine learning practitioners, and AI practitioners.

Databricks’ Developer Relations team is looking for a leader to manage our open source Developer Advocates, deepen our engagement across the Apache Software Foundation and Linux Foundation communities, and lead technical storytelling and experiences that strengthen trust and adoption. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in the spotlight, is known and respected in open source communities, and gets even more satisfaction from growing other advocates than from giving the keynote themselves.

As the Developer Advocate Manager for Open Source, you'll lead the team that advocates for the projects Databricks builds in the open, and serve as a crucial link between our engineering teams and the global community of practitioners building their careers on them. Your team's remit spans the Open Lakehouse — Apache Spark™ (including Spark Declarative Pipelines), Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Apache Iceberg™, and MLflow — as well as Omnigent, our open source meta-harness for composing, governing, and sharing AI agents. As the original creators of Apache Spark™, Delta Lake, and MLflow, we hold ourselves to a high standard here: our credibility in these communities is earned continuously, not inherited.

This role will leverage your expertise in building and scaling a developer relations team, and it will build on your standing within the open source world and your working relationships with the Apache Software Foundation, the Linux Foundation, and the maintainers and committers who keep these projects healthy. You'll coach your team on building a content flywheel — where a single demo, video, or talk becomes the source of truth for a dozen derivative assets — and on applying AI as a force multiplier without ever lowering the technical bar.

Your responsibilities will encompass both team leadership and a wide range of knowledge-sharing activities. You'll lead by example: delivering engaging talks, hosting panels and meetups, creating blogs and video content, developing courseware, answering questions in community forums, and meeting one-on-one with influential contributors and maintainers.

Community engagement will be at the heart of your role. You'll work closely with the open source communities and with product and engineering teams, ensuring that community needs and product development align seamlessly. Reporting directly to the Head of Developer Relations, you'll collaborate with fellow DevRel managers across our Databricks, App Dev, and DevRel Programs teams to create a cohesive and impactful open source strategy.

The ideal candidate embodies the values of our Developer Relations team: a deep passion for data and AI, genuine empathy for developers' needs, and a real, demonstrated commitment to open source — including the parts that don't directly benefit Databricks.

More about the DevRel team

The Developer Relations (DevRel) team at Databricks is dedicated to building and fostering relationships with communities of data practitioners. Our goal is to drive awareness and adoption of the Databricks Data + AI Platform — including Lakeflow, Lakebase, Genie Agents, and AI/BI — alongside the open source projects that underpin it, such as Apache Spark™, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, MLflow, Apache Iceberg™, and Omnigent. Our team also owns programs like the Databricks MVP program, the user group program, and DevConnect roadshows.

postings.description:
FEQ427R506

Team Overview & Mission

The FE Launchpad program builds a high-performing early-career Solutions Engineering team that delivers customer value at scale while developing the next generation of Solutions Architects at Databricks. Our team exists to strengthen the SA talent pipeline, expand impactful SA activities across broad customer use cases, and feed the field with fully ramped, high-impact SAs ready to drive immediate revenue results.

The Impact You Will Have

As the Program Lead for the FE Launchpad team, you will lead, coach, and mentor a team of early-career Solutions Engineers (SEs) through a 9-month learning and execution journey. You will balance hands-on talent development with operational leadership, partnering closely with Field Engineering (SA), Account Executive (AE), and Specialized Technical Specialist (STS) leadership to ensure seamless collaboration and tech win delivery via the ASQ (Architecture Support Queue) process.

Key responsibilities include:

- People Leadership & Talent Pipeline Development: Hire, coach, and mentor L3 Solutions Engineers. Build structured development plans to guide them from early-career professionals into independent, high-performing Senior Solutions Engineers.

- Operational & Technical Execution: Oversee team performance using the FE Launchpad Operational Dashboard. Manage funnel progression, activity tracking, account coverage, and technical evaluation quality across customer engagements.

- Cross-Functional Partnership: Establish tight alignment with SA, AE, and STS leadership in your territory to optimize ASQ workflow, match L3 capacity with field demand, and drive customer tech wins at scale.

- Technical & Pre-Sales Coaching: Conduct 1:1 coaching on technical discovery, requirement gathering, proof-of-concept (PoC) delivery, and communicating the business value of the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform.

- Program Execution: Oversee the execution of the 9-month FE Launchpad curriculum, tracking ramp milestones, technical certifications (AWS, Azure, GCP, Databricks), and readiness for promotion into regional field roles.

- People Management Experience: 2+ years leading pre-sales/solutions architecture teams, or 4+ years as a Senior/Principal Solutions Architect with a proven track record of mentoring early-career technical talent.

Mission

Databricks is seeking a Manager, Marketing Insights Business Partner to serve as the embedded insights partner to the [VP/GM] of EMEA Marketing and their leadership team. This role exists to create leverage: to make marketing performance easier to understand, easier to act on, and easier to improve.

Reporting to the Director, Marketing Insights, you will bring analytical rigor and a clear point of view to how EMEA plans, forecasts, measures, and improves its work. Beyond reporting on outcomes, you will produce the forecast leadership plans against, hold visibility into how the work itself is running, and help scope and land the pilots that change how we operate. You will partner closely with Marketing Leadership, Campaign Operations, Marketing Platform & Systems, Sales Operations and Finance.

- Serve as the insights partner to the [VP/GM] of EMEA Marketing and their leadership team, delivering the analysis and narrative required for business reviews, QBRs, and pipeline councils, so that leadership forums produce actionable decisions.

- Maintain the leading-indicator framework for EMEA, identifying the early signals that predict outcome performance, so that intervention happens while the quarter can still change, rather than being diagnosed after it closes.

- Translate performance data into insight, implications, and recommended areas of focus tied to internal milestones and supporting cross-functional requirements within regions.

- Own execution telemetry for EMEA, maintaining visibility into how marketing work is actually running through cycle times, throughput, intake, and SLA performance to reduce operational friction.

- Increase the region's self-sufficiency in accessing and using performance data by driving practical, repeatable adoption of Genie and reducing dependency on central data teams for routine reporting and analysis.

- Support pilot execution, defining the hypothesis, success criteria, and measurement approach before launch, and delivering a clear read at the end.

- Surface and codify what is already working in one market or motion so that proven approaches can be picked up elsewhere, and instrument them so the gain stays visible after the initial push.

- Support the planning cycle with the analytical & programmatic inputs that make investment decisions defensible, including historical performance, efficiency by motion, and target-setting inputs.

- Identify analytical and data risks early, including data quality issues, reporting gaps, and system performance outages, so they are surfaced and addressed before they escalate.

- Act as the region's voice in the global Marketing Insights function, surfacing regional requirements and gaps so that global frameworks and tooling work in-region rather than requiring local workarounds.
