postings.title: P2P Data & Automation Lead
postings.description:
GAQ327R181

While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations will be considered.

Databricks is executing a multi-year Procure-to-Pay transformation spanning an expense management platform migration, the BrickBuy enterprise procurement portal, a managed services onboarding, and policy and process redesign initiatives. This role sits embedded within Procurement — not in a central IT or analytics function — and operates in accordance with the Finance Data Strategy governance framework to drive rapid P2P process transformation by designing, deploying, and scaling automation and data solutions directly within business workflows.

This is a builder role for someone who wants to own outcomes, not tickets: the person will sit inside the processes they are automating, ship working solutions in weeks rather than quarters, and carry them through adoption — pairing hands-on technical delivery with the change management discipline needed to make new ways of working stick.

The impact you will have: 

- Business process ownership. Own designated P2P sub-processes end to end — intake-to-PO, invoice exception handling, supplier onboarding, expense workflows — including process mapping, baseline metrics (cycle time, touch rates, exception volumes), and redesign. Act as the recognized process owner who is accountable for how the process performs, not just how it is documented.

- Requirements & solution design. Translate pain points raised by requesters, approvers, buyers, and AP into structured requirements and solution designs. Work within the Finance Data Strategy governance framework for data definitions, source-of-truth alignment, access controls, and quality standards — solutions must tie to certified Finance data, not shadow datasets.

- Embedded automation. Design, deploy, and scale automations directly within business workflows and the systems where work actually happens (ZIP, SAP, NetSuite, expense platform, BrickBuy) — including AI/LLM-assisted triage, auto-routing, data enrichment, exception auto-resolution, and notification/nudge logic. Build in production-adjacent environments with appropriate guardrails rather than standalone tools users must remember to visit.

- Rapid iteration. Operate on a ship-measure-iterate cadence: release minimum viable automations in weeks, instrument them from day one, and refine based on usage data and user feedback. Maintain sandbox-to-production discipline consistent with Finance Data Strategy and SOX/control requirements.

- Data & measurement. Build and maintain the P2P datasets, dashboards, and metrics that the transformation runs on — cycle time, Fast Pass performance, first-pass yield, policy compliance, automation coverage, and adoption rates — and report against them in existing operating rhythms (e.g., quarterly business reviews), with numbers that tie across reports and to source data.

- User adoption & change management. Own the adoption of what you build. Design role-based training and enablement for affected requesters, approvers, and P2P operations staff; produce launch communications, FAQ/help content, and go-live announcements in a style consistent with executive reporting norms (concise, structured, blockers called out explicitly); run feedback loops with change champions across subsidiaries; and actively identify and mitigate resistance rather than assuming usage will follow deployment.

- Day-to-day prioritization. Run the intake and backlog for automation and data requests across Procurement: triage incoming asks, prioritize by value, effort, and risk, publish a visible roadmap, and make defensible trade-off calls daily — protecting capacity for transformation priorities while handling operational requests.

- Stakeholder engagement. Partner closely with Procurement operations, the Finance Data team, the CIO org, and managed services partners; represent Procurement in Finance Data Strategy governance forums; and ensure automation work lands coherently alongside parallel workstreams (expense platform migration, BrickBuy rollout, Global Procurement Policy adoption, managed services transition).

What we look for:

- 4–8 years in data analytics, process automation, or operations roles within P2P, procurement, or finance — with demonstrable examples of automations or data products you built, shipped, and scaled yourself.

- Hands-on technical skills: SQL and Python (or equivalent), workflow and integration tooling (iPaaS, RPA, or native platform automation), and dashboarding/BI. Experience building on the Databricks platform and applying LLM/AI tooling to business workflows is a strong plus.

- Working knowledge of P2P systems and data — ERP (SAP or NetSuite), procurement intake/orchestration platforms (ZIP or similar), and expense management tools — including how transactions, approvals, and master data flow between them.

- Experience operating within a data governance framework: certified data sources, data quality standards, access controls, and audit/SOX considerations — comfortable moving fast without going around governance.

- Change management fluency: track record of driving adoption of new tools or processes through training, communications, champion networks, and adoption metrics — not just deploying and moving on.

- Strong prioritization judgment and stakeholder management: able to run a busy intake, say no with a rationale, and communicate crisply to audiences from frontline requesters to executives.

- Experience in a high-growth, multi-entity organization (multiple subsidiaries/geographies) is a plus; formal change management certification (Prosci, ADKAR, or equivalent) or process improvement certification (Lean/Six Sigma) preferred but not required.

postings.description:
FEQ327R583

The Partner Enablement Operations Manager is a senior operator and builder responsible for designing and running a scalable, predictable, and data-driven operating model for partner enablement at Databricks.

This role serves as the operational backbone and strategic integrator for partner enablement, connecting global strategy to regional execution across AMER, EMEA, and APJ regions while ensuring programs are delivered consistently, efficiently, and at scale.

The ideal candidate brings strong executive presence, systems thinking, and a bias for automation. They know how to reduce operational friction, build governance that scales, and introduce AI-enabled workflows that improve responsiveness without adding unnecessary complexity or headcount.

We are looking for A builder who can architect operating systems, drive cross-functional alignment, and convert recurring operational friction into structural improvement.

What You’ll Do

- Own the partner enablement operating model, including core planning cadences, governance mechanisms, and execution frameworks that connect strategy to execution.

- Run QBRs, MBRs, and executive reviews for partner enablement leadership, using clear metrics and forward-looking insights to drive accountability and decision-making.

- Lead end-to-end execution of partner enablement initiatives, ensuring timelines, dependencies, and deliverables are managed effectively across functions and regions.

- Build and maintain dashboards and operating reviews that surface partner engagement, program performance, risk signals, and areas requiring intervention.

- Act as a key point of contact for cross-regional operational issues and escalations, resolving immediate friction while converting recurring issues into structural improvements.

- Design and implement scalable workflows, SOPs, SLAs, and intake mechanisms that improve consistency, reduce manual effort, and create a better experience for internal stakeholders and partners.

- Introduce AI-enabled and automation-first workflows for intake, reporting, support, certification, and partner operations where they can safely improve speed, quality, and scale.

- Collaborate closely with the Partner organization, Learning and Enablement, Professional Services, and other cross-functional teams to remove friction and improve execution across the partner ecosystem.

- Partner closely with the broader operations business to drive cross-functional leverage of ideas and excellence, ensuring new methods and operational innovations are scaled beyond just partner operations.

- Establish clear ownership models, decision rights, and governance guardrails to support regional nuance without creating shadow processes or operational inconsistencies.

- Architect and maintain automated intake management workflows and SLA tracking mechanisms to optimize request processing and eliminate wait-time bottlenecks.

- Establish standardized metric definitions and executive reporting frameworks that pair activity and outcome indicators to ensure reporting integrity across cross-functional teams.

What You Bring

Required Qualifications

- 10+ years of experience in Learning Operations, Program Management, Professional Services Operations, or a related operational leadership field in a high-growth technology environment.

- Proven experience supporting global or multi-region teams and translating central strategy into executable operating plans.

- Preferred experience in the Data & AI space, with a strong understanding of Databricks' platform capabilities, key differentiators, and end-to-end solutions, and the ability to work effectively with technical stakeholders.

- Demonstrated ownership of operating cadence, forecasting, planning, and execution frameworks in a complex, matrixed environment.

- Strong analytical capability and the ability to turn data into executive insight, operational decisions, and measurable business outcomes.

- Experience improving processes and workflows, with a clear track record of reducing manual effort and increasing scale through automation or AI-enabled solutions.

- Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions without direct authority.

- Ability to work independently, manage priorities across time zones, and drive execution in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

- Must be open to working a flexible schedule, including frequent late hours to accommodate discussions with the broader enablement team and partner liaisons, the majority of whom are based in the AMER timezone.

- Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional alignment and lead strategic delivery across matrixed global organizations.

- Experience designing and optimizing workflow automation, structured intake management, and operational reporting engines with strict metric definition discipline.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in partner enablement, customer education, learning operations, or training operations.

- Deep expertise working with and for System Integrators (SIs) and ISVs, with a strong grasp of their core operational principles and business models.

- Fluency with AI tools, workflow automation, and analytics platforms used to streamline operations and generate actionable insights.

- Strong commercial and operational acumen, including comfort with utilization, forecasting, partner spend, margin thinking, or RevOps-aligned execution.

- Experience operating in a highly matrixed international environment with sensitivity to regional and cultural nuance.

Why Join Us

You will play a central role in shaping how partner enablement scales at Databricks.

This is a high-visibility role with meaningful impact, offering the opportunity to build a more efficient, governed, and AI-enabled operating model that helps our partner ecosystem grow with the business.

If you enjoy turning ambiguity into structure, building systems that remove friction, and helping teams scale through better operations rather than more manual work, this role is for you.

Success Metrics

- Operational Predictability: Build a disciplined partner enablement operating cadence where risks are surfaced early and execution is measurable and consistent.

- Stakeholder Experience and Self-Sufficiency: Increase the percentage of standard partner enablement requests handled through structured, low-touch, or self-service workflows.

- Escalation Management and Process Resilience: Reduce recurring operational friction by improving escalation handling, clarifying ownership, and improving systemic resolution of recurring issues.

- Scalable Execution: Improve throughput, consistency, and delivery quality across global partner enablement programs without relying on incremental manual work.

- AI-Enabled Transformation: Deploy practical AI-enabled workflows that improve speed, visibility, and efficiency across intake, reporting, support, and partner operations.

postings.description:
Company Description:

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world’s toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world’s best data and AI platform, so our customers can focus on the high value challenges that are central to their own missions.

The Mosaic AI organization enables companies to develop AI models and systems using their own data, with technologies ranging from fine-tuning LLMs for enterprise domains, to a platform for building compound AI systems that use retrieval and agents. Mosaic AI is committed to the belief that a company’s AI models are just as valuable as any other core IP, and that high-quality AI models should be available to all.

Job description:

Most of the world's data+AI problems lie in enterprise domains, behind closed doors. Our research team's goal is to push the frontier of "domain adaptation" - how can we develop LLMs and AI systems that work well for custom domains. To do this we are tackling open research problems on a range of topics, from how to scale/automate eval, fine tune with synthetic data, retrieval augmentation, fast/efficient inference and more. 

You will work with our research team on projects focused on adapting LLMs and AI systems towards enterprise domains. This may include:

- Adapting, improving, and evaluating a method from the literature.

- Designing an entirely new method for domain adaptation.

- Composing together multiple methods to create new recipes for efficient post-training.

- Evaluation of LLMs and AI systems.

- Required:

- Research experience in and proficiency with the fundamentals of deep learning.

postings.title: Principal Brand Content & AI Search Visibility
postings.description:
MKTQ427R49

We're looking for a content lead who sits at the intersection of brand content storytelling and AI-era discoverability. You will own the creation of high-quality and high-volume brand content, ensuring that content is structured, distributed, and measured to win visibility across AI answer engines. You will produce and edit compelling content and employ optimization strategies to make sure LLMs discover, parse, and cite it. You will identify content gaps by analyzing where the brand is (and isn't) showing up in LLM answers, map those gaps against business objectives, target audiences, and product priorities, and orchestrate a mix of AI agents, technical writers, and internal teams to close them. A core part of this orchestration is overseeing a system of AI agents that create, optimize, and evaluate content — a task that requires real editorial expertise applied to prompt design and agent engineering, not just tool adoption. You will be responsible for building and maintaining the brand context, target prompts, and writing guidelines that guide agents and internal SMEs to create on-brand, accurate, and authoritative content. A major part of the role is editorial judgment: this includes reviewing drafts from agents and adjusting prompts and inputs to improve output quality.

The impact you will have:

Within 12–24 months in this role, success looks like:

- The content roadmap is driven by evidence. You've stood up ongoing GEO/AI answer analysis, and every major content bet ties back to a documented gap — where the brand is underrepresented, inaccurate, or absent — requiring gap-analysis skills and fluency with GEO/AI-visibility diagnostics.

- Business priorities and content output are in lockstep. The roadmap (blogs, video, web pages, thought leadership) is visibly built from business objectives, audience search intent, and product priorities, and stakeholders can trace any piece of content back to a prompt that justified it — requiring sharp prioritization judgment and the ability to translate business strategy into editorial direction.

- A multi-resource content engine runs smoothly. Agencies, freelance contractors, internal writers/producers, and AI content agents are each matched to the content types they're best suited for; workflows include adequate content review, and handoffs don't create bottlenecks — all of which require strong orchestration and tool/vendor/contributor management skills.

- Every piece of published content clears the bar you’ve set for that medium. You're the final editorial checkpoint on all content — agency, contractor, internal, or AI-generated — and your revision notes are specific enough to reliably lift drafts to brand standard, requiring proven editorial judgment across formats (long-form, blogs, video scripts, web copy).

- Content is winning visibility and citation share. Published content is structured to be entity-rich, answer-first, well-sourced, and citation-worthy for LLM retrieval, without losing readability or brand voice — requiring hands-on GEO/AEO expertise layered on solid SEO and writing fundamentals.

- Leadership can see the line from content to business outcome. You track GEO performance alongside traditional metrics and report on it regularly.

- The broader marketing team writes and creates with GEO/AI-visibility in mind by default. You've enabled marketers across the org on GEO prompts and tools, AI writing agents, brand context, and best practices for quality writing.

What we look for:

- 10+ years in content strategy, brand content, or editorial leadership, with experience managing a mix of internal and external contributors.

- Strong editorial judgment — proven ability to review and elevate drafts across formats to a consistent brand standard.

- Working knowledge of SEO fundamentals plus hands-on recent GEO/AEO experience — comfortable diagnosing why a brand isn't being cited or surfaced correctly by LLMs.

- Experience managing agencies and/or freelance contractors, and comfort building and optimizing AI content tools/agents as part of a production workflow.

- Familiarity with GEO/AI-visibility tools such as Profound, Conductor, AirOps, Peec.ai, or similar platforms.

- Proficiency with Semrush, Google Search Console, and Google Analytics (GA4) to track technical optimization and brand visibility in traditional search engines. 

- Sharp analytical instincts paired with strong creative/editorial taste.

- Experience in B2B tech, data/AI, or enterprise SaaS.

- Familiarity with schema markup and structured data for AI/search discoverability.

- Experience overseeing video production workflows.

postings.title: Principal Demand Generation Manager, Campaign Development
postings.description:
MKTQ227R22

The Principal Demand Generation Manager, Campaign Development, leads how Databricks plans and scales integrated marketing campaigns across the organization. This role defines the campaign framework and strategic guidance, and enables marketers to execute consistently. They are a key business SME that translates business needs into business requirements for campaign operations and planning tools.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Demand Generation, this role is responsible for uniting cross-functional stakeholders to develop and execute biannual, strategic, and integrated marketing plans across Demand Generation, Field Marketing, Corporate Events, Partner Marketing, and Industry. You’ll act as a central hub across various go-to-market teams—ensuring we align with the company's overarching priorities and deliver measurable growth.

The impact you will have:

- The CMO staff has timely, decision-ready visibility into campaign performance, program and investment shifts, and open questions requiring business guidance, enabling coordinated pivots as priorities change.
In partnership with Senior leadership, establishes a clear, repeatable integrated campaign framework; defining the primary GTM campaign themes, audience strategy, target setting, investment mix, channel activation, and regional business-unit planning requirements.
Every priority integrated campaign has a consistent, cross-functional plan that aligns audiences, business targets, investment allocation, channel activation, and regional execution before launch.
Marketers have practical strategic guidance, templates, and planning standards that improve consistency across campaigns while enabling campaign managers to make effective execution decisions.
Translates the campaign strategy into a business requirements documentation (BRD) that the Campaign Operations team can leverage when developing scalable processes, workflows, data fields, and operating capabilities.
Evolve planning processes to support more agile integrated campaign planning, clear feedback loops, and greater visibility into campaign readiness and performance.

What we look for:

- 7+ years of professional experience, including 5+ years in demand generation marketing within a high-growth company.

- Strong executive presence and communication skills with the ability to work with senior leadership to debate, drive decisions, and define clear expectations across the organization. 

- Experience developing, executing, and measuring integrated campaigns end-to-end, with the ability to connect strategy, audience, investment, activation, and performance.

- Proven ability to build operational frameworks, planning processes, templates, and feedback loops that drive consistent execution across a complex marketing organization.

- Demonstrated experience managing campaign investments and using performance analysis to guide prioritization, resource allocation, and business decisions.

- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional partners and senior leaders toward alignment and action.

- Ability to prioritize and deliver in a dynamic, fast-paced environment while managing competing priorities and adapting to changing business needs.

- Growth mindset and openness to fresh thinking, new ideas, and opportunities to improve how integrated campaigns are planned and delivered.

postings.description:
# P-725

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.

About the Team: Join the Core of Databricks Infrastructure

The Compute Infra Team is the engine behind all of Databricks' products and Control Plane services. We build and scale the foundational compute infrastructure that enables every Databricks customer to succeed, operating one of the largest and most dynamic data and AI clouds in the world.

Mission: Define the Future of Cloud Compute Efficiency and Scale

As the Technical Lead for Compute Fleet Management, you won't just manage a fleet—you will set the standard for how Databricks consumes and optimizes compute across all three major clouds (AWS, Azure, and GCP). This is a mission-critical role with direct impact on our gross margin and customer experience. Your mandate includes:

- Pioneering Fleet Optimization: Provisioning and pooling of O(Billion)s of cloud resources to achieve peak workload performance, industry-leading efficiency, and robust resource isolation.

- Delivering Hyper-Scale Resilience: Build the architecture that guarantees horizontal scaling and resilience against zonal or even cloud account-level failures, ensuring Databricks is always on.

- Owning the Critical Path: Lead the development of the lowest-dependency systems required to bootstrap and manage our massive compute platform.

Outcomes: The Impact You Will Deliver

This role is for an engineer who thrives on owning the most challenging and impactful outcomes:

- High Availability: Achieve and maintain 99.99% availability for all batch and serving workloads.

- Stellar Efficiency: Drive utilization to 60% or higher—a crucial metric that requires balancing high efficiency with unwavering tolerance for cloud failures.

- Best-in-Class Isolation: Architect and enforce strong security and performance isolation across a diverse range of customer workloads.

Requirements: Are You Ready for this Challenge?

We are seeking a seasoned Principal Engineer who has not only built but successfully operated large-scale, mission-critical infrastructure systems in production. You must have a track record of:

- Leading Transformative Projects: Taking ownership of complex, cross-team, cross-layer, and multi-quarter strategic engineering initiatives from concept to execution.

- Distributed Systems Mastery: Deep, hands-on experience developing and operating high-scale distributed systems on at least one major public cloud.

- Influence Without Authority: Proven ability to drive consensus, establish technical direction, and lead large technical efforts across organizational boundaries.

- Execution Discipline: Exceptional strength in planning, tracking project progress, and managing complex cross-organizational dependencies.

The Edge: Highly Desirable Experience

- Experience managing and scaling a massive fleet of GPUs for AI/ML workloads.

- Experience with developing and operating large-scale distributed systems across all major clouds (AWS, Azure, and GCP).

The Security Field Engineering team helps data teams solve the world's toughest problems by empowering customers to understand the security of the Databricks platform and by helping account teams address questions that come up during security reviews. About the role

AI is the defining platform shift of our generation, and Databricks is right at the center of it. We are looking for a Product Finance leader to scale the fastest growing part of our business with both speed and financial rigor. You will be the primary finance partner to our AI Engineering and Product leaders, with a mandate that spans the full arc of the AI business: planning GPU supply and demand across clouds, shaping how we price AI products, and building the unit economics that will define the margins of this category for years to come. 

The impact you will have

- Plan the GPU supply and demand that powers the business

- Establish a trusted, unified GPU demand plan across production inference, internal research, and new product bets so we invest ahead of growth without over-provisioning.

- Drive capacity commitment and procurement strategies across major hyperscalers and emerging neoclouds, optimizing the mix of reserved, spot, and on-demand compute.

- Own AI product economics and partner on pricing

- Lead revenue and margin analytics across the AI product portfolio, turning raw consumption telemetry into a clear read on customer adoption, retention, and product profitability.

- Model the end-to-end unit economics of AI products before they ship, partnering with Product and Pricing to design consumption structures that drive adoption while protecting gross margin targets.

- Run tight financial operations, from auditable multi-cloud cost allocation to automated reporting, giving product and engineering leaders real-time visibility into their economic goals.

- Bring finance rigor to the biggest investment decisions

- Build, mentor, and scale a high-performing team of product finance analysts capable of operating at the intersection of deep technical infrastructure and commercial strategy

What we look for

Required

- 10+ years of experience in Strategic/Product Finance, complemented by foundational training in Investment Banking, Private Equity, or Management Consulting.

- Deep fluency in consumption-based business models, public cloud infrastructure costs, unit cost analysis, and gross margin optimization.

- A proven track record of partnering directly with senior Engineering and Product executives to influence technical roadmaps and commercial pricing.

postings.description:
(GAQ427R230)

About the role As customers build their mission-critical data and AI workloads on Databricks, our shared cloud platform infrastructure is scaling at unprecedented speed. We are looking for a Product Finance Senior Manager to own the economics and financial operations of our multi-cloud platform spend. You will be a key finance partner to our Cloud Engineering and Infrastructure Operations leaders, with a mandate that spans driver-based cloud forecasting, infrastructure efficiency roadmaps, and scalable cost attribution across our product portfolio.

The impact you will have

- Drive analytics and modeling to understand how platform spend scales

- Lead deep data analytics to identify the underlying drivers of shared cloud platform spend across products, cloud providers, and global regions.

- Build robust, driver-based forecasting models that accurately predict infrastructure spend across regional expansion, customer scale, and new product launches.

- Partner with Cloud Infrastructure Operations to design a forward-looking cost attribution model that accurately maps shared platform expenses to individual products.

- Establish robust KPIs and operations to achieve unit economics goals

- Partner with Engineering to define north star efficiency KPIs across core platform services and storage/compute layers.

- Build the infrastructure efficiency roadmap alongside Engineering and translate technical optimizations into committed operating and gross margin targets.

- Drive tight operational rhythms and reporting so product and engineering leaders have clear visibility to execute against their unit economic goals.

- Scale cloud finance operations and systems

- Bring systems-level thinking to cloud FP&A processes, building automated workflows that scale as our multi-cloud footprint and commitment structures become increasingly dynamic.

- Ensure cloud cost allocation frameworks, monthly accruals, and reporting pipelines remain rigorous, auditable, and scalable as the business compounds.

- Dogfood the Databricks platform to analyze massive cloud billing and telemetry datasets, delivering self-serve cost visibility to engineering partners.

What we look for

- Required

- 8+ years of experience in Strategic/Product Finance, Cloud FP&A, or FinOps, complemented by foundational training in Investment Banking, Consulting, or high-growth technology.

- Deep fluency in consumption-based business models, public cloud infrastructure costs (AWS, Azure, GCP), unit cost analysis, and gross margin drivers.

- A proven track record of partnering directly with Engineering and Cloud Infrastructure Operations teams to drive cost efficiency and forecasting accuracy.

- Systems-level thinker with a demonstrated ability to build scalable financial processes, driver-based models, and auditable allocation frameworks in fast-moving environments.

- Preferred

- Functional expertise in hyperscaler cloud pricing, enterprise commitment structures, and infrastructure deal economics.

- Experience attributing shared platform or foundational infrastructure costs across a multi-product SaaS or PaaS portfolio.

- Hands-on proficiency with SQL, Python, or notebook environments (especially Databricks) to self-serve insights from massive cloud billing and usage datasets.

postings.description:
GAQ427R57

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including over 70% of the Fortune 500 and most of the largest U.S. government agencies — rely on Databricks to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics, and agents.

About the Role

As a Program Manager for Public Sector in Commercial Legal at Databricks, you will own the contracting engine for one of the fastest-growing segments of the business: US and international public-sector deals. Reporting to the Director & Associate General Counsel, Commercial, you will act as the operational backbone for the public-sector contracting function, working in close coordination with Public Sector legal, sales, operations, product, engineering, finance, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

This is a mission-critical and highly independent role designed for a proactive, focused person who thrives on building programs in-flight to drive accountability and positive, timely outcomes. You won't just track workstreams — you will own them. You will design and manage contracting programs and workflows, build playbooks and governance frameworks, route and manage complex government deals through stakeholders, handle routine contracting matters under attorney supervision, and support some contract management/contract lifecycle work (including Databricks' GSA MAS). - Government Contracting Substance: 6+ years in government contracts, public procurement, or contract administration at a technology company (required). Bonus if you've previously been a COR/COTR. - SaaS & Cloud Contracting Fluency: Experience with subscription/consumption-based SaaS agreements and interactions with finance, deal desk, and security/product/privacy terms. You understand how commercial cloud contracting intersects with government procurement requirements.

postings.description:
About the role

Databricks bills customers on usage. Every month, millions of usage records turn into commit drawdowns, invoices and revenue. The Revenue Operations team within Order to Cash organization makes sure that happens accurately and on time.

We’re hiring a Revenue Operations Manager to oversee usage operations and improve how contracts move from booking to invoicing. A key focus is Universal Commitment, our cloud-agnostic commit model. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Revenue Operations, you’ll lead key month-end close activities for our billing and rating platform, oversee a team based in India, and drive process and automation improvements across Revenue Operations. 

You'll work closely with the Order to Revenue Process Compliance team. That team sets usage policy, leads root-cause analysis and owns governance. Your team carries out the work: applying adjustments, keeping usage and billing in balance, and making sure each correction is documented, reviewed and fully reflected in our systems.

What you'll do

Revenue operations and contract setup

- Own the booking review process. Validate orders in the booking queue and serve as the escalation point for upstream teams on complex contract structures.

- Make sure contract and usage settings are correct across our billing and rating platform, ERP and CPQ, so that Universal Commitment and other contract type invoice as intended.

- Advise Deal Desk and Revenue Assurance on whether non-standard terms can be billed (e.g., GPU reservations, per-hour pricing, custom SKUs) before deals close. Provide guidance on new product offerings and ensure operational feasibility prior to finance sign off.

- Define and report Revenue Operations KPIs, such as adjustment volume, close timeliness, and billing accuracy.

Usage operations and adjustments

- Oversee and approve usage adjustments, billing corrections and customer credits in DBAR and the ERP. This covers billing errors, SLA credits and customer satisfaction (CSAT) credits, in line with Usage Compliance policies and approval levels.

- Serve as the escalation point for manual usage processing, including manual usage uploads, reservation and non-standard billing, ledger entries, and retract-and-restate corrections, with a full audit trail.

- Make sure usage-to-contract mapping, including customer workspace moves, PAYG-to-commit conversions and mid-term contract changes, with the correct effective dates.

- Act as the Revenue Operations owner of the refund and credit process, from intake, and validation through execution.

- Approve or deny account provisioning requests (suspend, unsuspend, grace-period extensions) with the Network Operations Center (NOC).

- Oversee usage tracking for customers with special provisions and non-standard language in their order form.

Month-end and quarter-end close

- Lead our contract reconciliation which ingests and compares usage across all clouds at the contractual level. Partner with Engineering, from pre-close through delivery of the final usage file to Revenue Accounting .

- Run usage categorization and commit and PAYG reconciliations, between the billing platform and the ERP across all clouds.

- Own billing finalization (Billing Mass Finalization / ledger freeze), the step that closes each month.

- Partner with the Revenue Accounting on usage flux analysis and contribute to shorten the close timeline.

- Act as preparer and/or reviewer for assigned SOX controls (e.g., usage reconciliation and SKU pricing accuracy) and keep audit evidence ready.Align with RevOps team to continue to improve recon process by assimilating processes across all clouds. Oversee Universal Commit contract reconciliation to ensure completeness.

Team leadership and scale

- Lead and develop the GBS usage team (India). Set priorities, review work, and steadily expand team ownership.Write, maintain and centrally store SOPs for every recurring process, and make sure each critical close task has a trained backup.

- Use SQL and Databricks dashboards to automate reconciliations and reduce manual effort, working toward touchless billing.

Cross-functional partnership

- Partner with the Usage Compliance team. Hand off recurring adjustment patterns and supporting data for root-cause analysis, put new policies into practice, and report adjustment volume and status.

- Work with the Money/DBAR Engineering, IT/Business Systems, Deal Desk, Billing, Collections and Revenue Accounting teams to resolve usage and billing issues quickly.

- 

- Serve as subject matter expert on strategic initiatives and projects by working with our commercialization team, engineering, and other GTM and Accounting teams. Will require driving project initiatives in certain cases.

What we're looking for

Required

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related field.

- 6+ years in revenue operations, billing operations or order-to-cash, ideally with usage- or consumption-based billing.

- 2+ years managing people, including leading offshore or shared-service teams.

- Hands-on experience with billing or rating systems and a major ERP (e.g., SAP, NetSuite or Oracle), plus Salesforce/CPQ.

- Strong SQL skills. Experience with Databricks is a plus.

- Track record of running month-end close tasks on time, with SOX controls.

- Experience leading or guiding offshore or shared-services teams.

- Clear written communication and a habit of documenting your work and sharing knowledge openly.

Nice to have

- Experience with commit, drawdown and burst contract models, or cloud marketplace billing (AWS, Azure, GCP).

- Working knowledge of usage-based revenue recognition (ASC 606).

- Experience with system migrations or parallel runs for billing or ERP platforms.

postings.title: SAP Functional SME
postings.description:
GAQ226R76

About Databricks

At Databricks, our mission is to help data teams solve the world's toughest problems—and that begins with empowering our own employees with exceptional internal products. The Databricks IT organization is a product-led engineering team building intelligent, AI-powered platforms that simplify how work gets done across the company. For Finance, our vision is to eliminate manual, repetitive work by automating complex business processes, surfacing actionable insights, and orchestrating end-to-end workflows. We are reimagining finance operations so teams spend less time processing transactions, chasing approvals, and resolving exceptions, and more time delivering strategic insights that accelerate the business.

We're looking for an SAP Functional SME to own the functional design of our core finance processes on S/4HANA and to shape how AI and agentic automation reimagine them. In this role, you'll be the deep functional authority for your domain—translating how the business actually runs into standard, clean-core S/4HANA solutions, using process intelligence to find what's broken, and defining where AI belongs in a controlled, auditable process. You'll work at the intersection of SAP and AI, bridging Finance and Engineering to deliver a simpler, smarter, more automated experience.

The Opportunity

SAP will serve as the foundation for Databricks' core finance processes, including Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, and Order-to-Cash. As the SAP Functional SME, you'll own the functional blueprint for those processes—leading discovery and AS-IS/TO-BE design, configuring S/4HANA, and defining the requirements for the intelligent, agentic layer that automates routine work and guides users through exceptions and approvals. You'll use process mining and business process intelligence to quantify opportunity and prioritize what to build, and you'll make the call on where AI-driven recommendations belong versus deterministic rules. Your mission is to combine deep functional expertise with the power of Databricks AI to create a modern, highly automated finance experience that lets the business scale.

What You'll Do

- Own Functional Design: Lead end-to-end process discovery and AS-IS/TO-BE design for major finance processes (Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, Order-to-Cash), define S/4HANA solution scope, and design to standard, clean-core capabilities wherever possible.

- Configure S/4HANA: Own functional configuration, business rules, and master-data strategy for your domain, and partner with developers on extensions, APIs, and orchestration where standard functionality falls short.

- Drive Process Intelligence: Use process mining and business process intelligence (leveraging SAP Process Intelligence and related tools) to identify root causes, quantify opportunity, and prioritize improvements; translate those findings into concrete S/4HANA requirements.

- Shape the AI & Agentic Layer: Define the requirements for AI-assisted and agentic process improvements—task automation, intelligent recommendations, anomaly detection, and generative assistants—and make clear judgments about where AI belongs in a controlled, auditable process, where human-in-the-loop is required, and where a deterministic rule is the better answer.

- Bridge Business and Engineering: Serve as the connective tissue between Finance process owners and the engineering pods, partnering with architects and developers to embed AI safely and to define the data flows between S/4HANA, process intelligence tools, SAP BTP, and Databricks AI.

- Run Workshops and Validate Value: Facilitate stakeholder workshops to validate business value, define acceptance criteria, and lead user acceptance testing for both functional and AI features.

- Measure Outcomes: Define KPIs and track ROI for process improvements—cycle time, touchless transaction rate, exception and manual-touch reduction, adoption—and build the business cases for prioritized automation and AI initiatives.

- Enable Adoption: Coach and upskill process owners and functional teams on process intelligence, best practices, and AI adoption, and drive readiness and change management for what you ship.

What You Bring

- 6+ years of SAP functional consulting experience, with hands-on delivery across at least one full S/4HANA lifecycle and deep expertise in one or more finance domains—Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, or Order-to-Cash—plus working fluency in adjacent areas and in master-data governance.

- Process Intelligence: Demonstrated experience leading process discovery, process mapping, and process mining using SAP Process Intelligence or equivalent BPI tools, and translating mining outputs into solution requirements.

- Clean-Core Mindset: Strong bias toward standard, clean-core S/4HANA design, with sound judgment about when a requirement genuinely warrants an extension versus a change in process.

- AI & Agentic Automation: Practical experience applying Databricks AI and agentic capabilities to enterprise processes, with strong judgment on where AI can drive automation and decision support while maintaining appropriate governance, controls, auditability, and human oversight.

- Integration Awareness: Solid understanding of integration patterns (APIs/OData, IDoc, SAP Integration Suite / BTP) and the data requirements that feed process mining and AI models.

- Governance Rigor: Working knowledge of SAP authorizations, SoD, SOX and audit requirements, and the ability to design processes and automation that satisfy them.

- Stakeholder Leadership: Excellent workshop facilitation, stakeholder management, and change-management skills, and the ability to present executive-level ROI and translate technical capability into measurable business value.

- Business-First Mindset: Pragmatic, outcome-driven approach to reducing process waste and risk, and comfort leading through ambiguity across complex business and IT landscapes.

Preferred Qualifications

- SAP S/4HANA Associate or Professional certification for a relevant module, and SAP Activate methodology experience.

- Certification or training in SAP Process Intelligence, or experience with Celonis or other process mining vendors.

- Hands-on experience delivering at least one AI-assisted process improvement in production.

- Familiarity with the SAP AI and extension stack (BTP, AI Core, Joule) and a point of view on build-versus-adopt tradeoffs against a Databricks-native approach.

- Experience working alongside data teams to make ERP data usable for analytics and AI on modern data platforms (such as Databricks), and prior work in a high-growth technology company where ERP had to scale quickly.

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. At Databricks, our mission is to help data teams solve the world's toughest problems—and that begins with empowering our own employees with exceptional internal products. We're looking for an SAP Technical Lead to own the technical architecture and delivery of our SAP platform. In this role, you'll define the technical vision for a clean-core S/4HANA landscape, lead the engineers who build on it, and architect the intelligent, agentic AI layer that sits between SAP and the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You'll set the standards, make the hard build-versus-adopt calls, and ensure everything we ship is secure, performant, and built to scale.

The Opportunity

SAP will serve as the foundation for Databricks' core finance processes, including Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, and Order-to-Cash. As the SAP Technical Lead, you will own how those processes are engineered—from the clean-core S/4HANA core and its extensions, to the integration fabric that connects SAP to the rest of the enterprise, to the AI and agentic services that make the experience intelligent. Rather than accumulating custom code inside the digital core, you'll champion a modern extensibility model on SAP BTP and the Databricks Lakehouse, so Finance teams get automated, AI-driven workflows on top of a core that stays clean, upgradable, and fast. Your mission is to combine the strength of SAP with the power of Databricks AI to build a technical foundation that lets the business scale.

What You'll Do

- Own the Technical Architecture: Define and own the end-to-end technical architecture for the S/4HANA landscape (greenfield, brownfield, or selective data transition), aligned to clean-core principles, with clear guardrails that keep the digital core standard and upgrade-ready.

- Lead the Extensibility Strategy: Define and own the extensibility strategy for SAP, using Databricks-native applications to address business requirements beyond core SAP capabilities. Establish clear architecture and governance standards to ensure extensions are scalable, secure, and aligned with the broader Finance technology strategy.

- Drive Enterprise AI Integration: Drive a strong integration with ongoing Enterprise AI transformation within Databricks by bringing AI fluency and hands on AI experience.

- Design the Integration Fabric: Architect secure, resilient integration across SAP and non-SAP systems using SAP Integration Suite, event-driven patterns, APIs, OData v4, and change-data feeds into the Lakehouse, with clear contracts, error handling, and observability.

- Unify SAP Data in the Lakehouse: Partner with data engineering on the technical patterns for landing SAP data in Databricks—ingestion, CDC, semantic and master-data modeling, lineage, and governance.

- Set Engineering Standards: Establish CI/CD, automated testing, and transport/deployment pipelines for BTP artifacts; own code and design reviews; and define the technical standards, security patterns, and best practices the team builds against.

- Lead the Team: Mentor developers and architects, lead technical steering, and act as the connective tissue across the SAP ecosystem (BTP, Integration Suite) and the systems around it, partnering closely with functional, product, and partner engineering teams.

- Be Accountable for Non-Functionals: Own performance, scalability, security, resilience, and cost across the landscape; report technical status, risks, and roadmaps to stakeholders.

What You Bring

- 10+ years in SAP technical roles, with 3+ years as a technical lead or architect, and a proven track record delivering at least one full S/4HANA program (greenfield or conversion) plus BTP-based extension delivery.

- Clean-Core Architecture: Deep, hands-on command of clean-core principles—custom-code assessment and remediation, in-app vs. side-by-side extensibility, released APIs and extension points, and the governance that keeps the core clean over time.

- SAP BTP & Modern Development: Advanced experience across SAP BTP, ABAP Cloud and the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP), CDS, and CAP, with Fiori/SAPUI5 on the front end.

- AI & Agentic Systems: Hands-on experience or strong technical command of agentic automation, LLM orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation—plus clear judgment about where AI belongs in a controlled, auditable ERP process and where it does not.

- Integration & APIs: Advanced experience with SAP Integration Suite, API management, event-driven architecture, and REST/OData, integrating hybrid SAP and non-SAP landscapes.

- Data Fluency: Solid understanding of modern data platforms, SAP data extraction and modeling, pipelines, and semantic layers, and the practical work of making ERP data usable for analytics and AI.

- Governance Rigor: Working knowledge of SAP authorizations, SoD, SOX and audit requirements, and the ability to architect solutions and automation that satisfy them.

- Leadership: Ability to translate business requirements into technical architecture, present tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders, mentor engineers, and make pragmatic decisions that balance speed against long-term maintainability.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience building custom applications or automation layers on modern data platforms (such as Databricks) that extend or sit alongside SAP.

- A clear point of view on build-versus-adopt tradeoffs across the SAP AI and extension stack (BTP, AI Core, Joule) versus a Databricks-native approach.

Meeting Operations & Event Execution

postings.title: Senior Compensation Manager, GTM
postings.description:
(GAQ327R299)

Databricks is looking for a strategic compensation leader who likes to build. You'll be a trusted partner to founders and senior leadership in our Go-To-Market (GTM) organization. You'll work with them to create compensation solutions that help us attract, retain and motivate world-class GTM talent, and you'll use AI to build the tools that make those solutions scale. This role reports to the Director of Compensation.

At Databricks, we don't think of compensation as just a number. It's how we recognize that every employee is an owner and part of our success. We're looking for someone with a strong foundation and a track record of doing exactly that.

What it takes to thrive

Databricks is a deeply technical, fast-moving environment, and our GTM organization is a key engine of our growth. You'll partner with dynamic, data-driven leaders who value rigorous analysis, clear perspectives, and collaborative problem-solving. In this role, priorities can evolve quickly, and you'll often navigate multiple important initiatives at once.

We set high standards for this role to support our fast-paced growth. Successful team members in this environment tend to:

- Build trust through analytical rigor. You present well-reasoned models and effectively articulate complex analysis to quantitative leaders.

- Navigate fast-paced priorities with resilience. You maintain focus, sound judgment, and positivity when balancing competing deadlines and feedback.

- Offer constructive perspectives. You confidently partner with senior stakeholders to propose data-backed alternative solutions and drive alignment to finalize decisions.

- Embrace feedback as a growth tool. You extract actionable insights from feedback and respond with clarity and openness.

- Create order from ambiguity. When there's no playbook, you build one, and you're comfortable acting on 80% of the information.

If you are excited by high standards, technical depth, and collaborative strategic discussions, you will find this work deeply rewarding.

The impact you will have

This is a hands-on, high-impact role. Expected time on each area:

GTM compensation solutions and strategic advice (40%)

- Work directly with GTM leaders to diagnose talent challenges such as competitive attrition, hard-to-fill roles, rapid scaling and reorganizations, and design attraction and retention solutions that fix them.

- Turn vague or urgent requests into clear options with explicit tradeoffs, then help leaders reach a decision.

- Serve as the main compensation advisor on strategic executive hires and high-stakes retention situations.

AI-enabled lifecycle compensation (30%)

- Run merit, refresh equity and promotion cycles end to end for global GTM teams.

- Design and build AI tools and workflows that reduce manual work and improve decisions. Examples include offer modeling, retention-risk analysis, cycle quality checks, and self-serve insights for leaders.

- Spot what's repetitive or error-prone in today's processes and automate it.

Enterprise compensation frameworks (30%)

- Help scale Databricks' global compensation structure, including market pricing models, pay-for-performance design and equity strategy.

- Build frameworks that solve today's problems and anticipate the ones coming as we grow.

What we look for

Quantitative and technical skill is the foundation of this role. Everything else we look for builds on it.

1. Quantitative and technical foundation (required)

- Expert-level analytical modeling. You build compensation models from scratch, including cost-of-program scenarios, pay-positioning analysis, attrition and retention-risk modeling, and sensitivity and tradeoff analysis. 

- Built with AI. You've personally used AI tools (for example LLMs, AI assistants, or automation and agent platforms) to build compensation tools, models or workflows that others rely on. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to explain how it works, what you'd improve, and how you checked that its outputs were accurate.

- Equity fluency. You understand RSU and option mechanics, vesting design, refresh strategy, and how grant values and share price movement affect cost and retention.

- Statistical judgment. You know when a market data cut is credible, when a sample is too small, and how to present ranges and market pricing without false precision.

2. Compensation expertise (required)

- You know your craft. Job architecture, compensation frameworks, market pricing, year-end and mid-year pay cycles, global compensation practices, and pay-for-performance design.

- You know the competition. Deep knowledge of competitor compensation, especially new-hire and refresh equity strategy at high-growth and public tech companies.

- You reason from first principles. You balance compensation best practice with what the business actually needs, and you can rebuild a framework from its underlying logic when the standard approach doesn't fit.

3. Strategic partnership (required)

- Trusted advisor to senior leaders. You have a track record of advising executives on sensitive, high-stakes compensation decisions (offers, promotions, leveling, retention, transfers, org changes) and influencing the outcome through data and judgment rather than authority.

- Operational excellence. You connect the dots between systems, stakeholders and programs to deliver compensation programs end to end, accurately and on time.

- Clear communicator. You turn complex analysis into a crisp recommendation an executive can act on in one conversation.

Nice-to-haves

- Experience with Tableau or other BI tools, or building dashboards for leaders.

- Experience supporting GTM or sales organizations at a high-growth tech company.

- Experience scaling compensation programs through hypergrowth, IPO, or major organizational change.

- A background in a quantitative field (for example finance, statistics, engineering), or equivalent experience.

You will define how the agents retrieve, reason over, and surface enablement insights to global Account Teams, turning learner and account data into prescriptive, just-in-time recommendations that improve account health and grow the number of trained users across our customer base. 

By automating GTM processes, you will ensure Account Teams and customers receive consistent Databricks enablement planning resources. You will be responsible for driving the AI roadmap for customer enablement, compounding enablement as a strategic leverage for our customers and for Databricks. 

This role will report to the Global Customer Enablement Practice Senior Director. This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated and innovative entrepreneur with a passion for working across departments and across regions.

- Own the product roadmap and architecture direction for the Scaled Customer Enablement Agent Suite — defining the data inputs, retrieval sources, and agent behaviors that generate enablement recommendations.

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, California to a global organization with over 1000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest growing SaaS companies in the world.

Our engineering teams build highly technical products that fulfill real, important needs in the world. We constantly push the boundaries of data and AI technology, while simultaneously operating with the resilience, security and scale that is critical to making customers successful on our platform.

We develop and operate one of the largest scale software platforms. The fleet consists of millions of virtual machines, generating terabytes of logs and processing exabytes of data per day. At our scale, we regularly observe cloud hardware, network, and operating system faults, and our software must gracefully shield our customers from any of the above.

The impact you will have:

- Shape the direction of some of our key data science areas for 2020 - usage forecasting, product analytics, user behavior and funnel analysis.

- Manage stakeholders for their focus area - gather changing requirements, define project OKRs and milestones, and communicate progress and results to a non-technical audience.

- Mentor and guide data-scientists on the team by helping with project planning, technical decisions, and code and document review.

- Build self-serving internal data products to make data simple within the company.

What we look for:

- Experience in applying Data Science / ML in production to build data-driven products for solving business problems.

postings.description:
CSQ227R215

As a Senior Designated Engineer and tech subject matter expert, you will partner closely with our Field and Engineering teams to deliver high-touch specialized support and tailored technical solutions for Databricks' largest and most strategic customers in the Digital Native Business (DNB) segment. In this customer-facing role, you will leverage your technical expertise in Apache Spark™ and other data technologies to triage and resolve complex product issues and unblock our customers’ most critical technical challenges. 

The Impact You Will Have:

- Perform advanced Troubleshooting and Root Cause Analysis to resolve performance and reliability issues in Spark, SQL, Delta, Streaming, and Databricks runtime features using tools like Spark UI metrics, Mosaic AI Model Service, DAGs, and event logs.

- Discover requirements for continuous monitoring to detect early performance issues, working with R&D and NOC teams to optimise the DNB customer environments. 

- Build Rapid POCs, Test/Deploy/Monitor the solutions built by Databricks Engineering to address customer challenges and showcase advanced Spark/ML/AI runtime capabilities aligned with their business goals.

- Develop comprehensive playbooks and maintain a knowledge base of common issues and solutions for Spark, ML, and AI workflows.

- Train customer engineering and business teams on best practices in performance tuning, debugging, and effectively leveraging Databricks Features.

- Pilot new best practices processes/ programs, champion process improvements, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to enhance the customer experience.

- Advocate for customers in business review meetings and maintain close relationships as a trusted advisor and primary technical point of contact.

- Collaborate onsite with Field Engineering, Sales, and Product teams during customer engagements and technical presentations to provide rapid solutions to production-impacting issues, demonstrating deep technical expertise and building strong customer trust.

What We Look For:

- Technical Expertise in Big Data and Spark: 5 to 8 years of experience designing, building, and troubleshooting distributed computing applications, with 4+ years delivering production-scale Spark/ML/AI solutions using Python, Java, or Scala.

- Data Engineering Specialisation: Hands-on expertise with Data Lakes, SQL-based databases, and Cloud-based Data Warehousing/ETL tools like Snowflake, Redshift, Bigquery, etc

- Advanced Tech Skills: Deep knowledge of Spark core internals, Delta/Iceberg, JVM optimisation, and memory management, with additional proficiency in AI ecosystems like Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Generative AI.

- Cloud and CI/CD Skills: Practical experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP, coupled with expertise in building and managing CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and alerting systems.

- Customer-Facing Experience: 3–5 years in customer-facing roles such as Technical Account Manager or Solutions Architect, demonstrating strong communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.

- Advanced Proactive Problem Solving Skills: Proven ability to anticipate, identify, and mitigate risks while planning solutions for production challenges. Effectively use sound business judgment, risk avoidance and subject matter expert resources to coordinate team efforts to solve problems.

postings.title: Senior Manager Compensation R&D
postings.description:
GAQ127R143

Databricks is looking for a strategic compensation leader who likes to build. You'll be a trusted partner to founders and senior leaders in our Engineering organization. Together you'll create compensation solutions that help us attract, retain and motivate world-class engineering and technical talent, and you'll use AI to build the tools that make those solutions scale. This role reports to the Director of Compensation.

At Databricks, compensation is more than a number. It's how we show that every employee is an owner and part of our success. We're looking for someone with a strong foundation and a track record of doing exactly that.

What it takes to thrive

Databricks is a deeply technical, fast-moving company, and our Engineering organization builds the platform everything else runs on. You'll partner with highly technical, data-driven leaders who expect rigorous analysis, clear points of view and collaborative problem-solving. Priorities can change quickly, and you'll often run several important initiatives at once.

We set high standards for this role to support our fast-paced growth. Successful team members in this environment tend to:

- Build trust through analytical rigor. You present well-reasoned models and effectively articulate complex analysis to engineering leaders who will test your assumptions.

- Navigate fast-paced priorities with resilience. You maintain focus, sound judgment, and positivity when balancing competing deadlines and feedback.

- Offer constructive perspectives. You confidently partner with senior stakeholders to propose data-backed alternative solutions and drive alignment to finalize decisions.

- Embrace feedback as a growth tool. You extract actionable insights from feedback and respond with clarity and openness.

- Create order from ambiguity. When there's no playbook, you build one, and you're comfortable acting on 80% of the information.

If you are excited by high standards, technical depth, and collaborative strategic discussions, you will find this work deeply rewarding.

The impact you will have

This is a hands-on, high-impact role. Expected time on each area:

Engineering compensation solutions and strategic advice (40%)

- Work directly with Engineering leaders to diagnose talent challenges, such as competition for AI/ML and infrastructure talent, hard-to-fill specialist roles, rapid team scaling, acquisitions and reorganizations. Then design attraction and retention solutions that solve them.

- Turn vague or urgent requests into clear options with explicit tradeoffs, and help leaders reach a decision.

- Serve as the main compensation advisor on strategic technical hires (senior ICs, distinguished engineers, research leaders and engineering executives) and on high-stakes retention cases.

- Advise on technical leveling, including IC and management career paths and how compensation should differ across them.

AI-enabled lifecycle compensation (30%)

- Run merit, refresh equity and promotion cycles end to end for global R&D teams.

- Design and build AI tools and workflows that reduce manual work and improve decisions. Examples include offer modeling, retention-risk analysis, cycle quality checks, and self-serve insights for leaders.

- Spot what's repetitive or error-prone in today's processes and automate it.

Enterprise compensation frameworks (30%)

- Help scale Databricks' global compensation structure, including market pricing models, pay-for-performance design, equity strategy and technical job architecture.

- Build frameworks that solve today's problems and anticipate the ones coming as we grow, including emerging skill premiums such as AI/ML.

What we look for

Quantitative and technical skill is the foundation of this role. Everything else we look for builds on it.

1. Quantitative and technical foundation (required)

- Expert-level analytical modeling. You build compensation models from scratch, including cost-of-program scenarios, pay-positioning analysis, attrition and retention-risk modeling, and sensitivity and tradeoff analysis. 

- Built with AI. You've personally used AI tools (for example LLMs, AI assistants, or automation and agent platforms) to build compensation tools, models or workflows that others rely on. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to explain how it works, what you'd improve, and how you checked that its outputs were accurate.

- Equity fluency. You understand RSU and option mechanics, vesting design, refresh strategy, and how grant values and share price movement affect cost and retention, especially for long-tenured, high-equity technical talent.

- Statistical judgment. You know when a market data cut is credible, when a sample is too small (common with niche technical roles), and how to present ranges and market pricing without false precision.

2. Compensation expertise (required)

- You know your craft. Job architecture, technical career ladders, compensation frameworks, market pricing, year-end and mid-year pay cycles, global compensation practices, and pay-for-performance design.

- You know the competition. Deep knowledge of competitor compensation for high-tech talent, especially new-hire and refresh equity strategy at high-growth tech companies, public tech companies, and AI labs.

- You reason from first principles. You balance compensation best practice with what the business actually needs, and you can rebuild a framework from its underlying logic when the standard approach doesn't fit.

3. Strategic partnership (required)

- Trusted advisor to senior leaders. You have a track record of advising executives on sensitive, high-stakes compensation decisions (offers, promotions, leveling, retention, transfers, org changes) and influencing the outcome through data and judgment rather than authority.

- Operational excellence. You connect the dots between systems, stakeholders and programs to deliver compensation programs end to end, accurately and on time.

- Clear communicator. You turn complex analysis into a crisp recommendation an executive can act on in one conversation.

Nice-to-haves

- Experience supporting Engineering, R&D or other technical organizations at a high-growth tech company.

- Familiarity with the market for AI/ML, research or specialized infrastructure talent.

- Experience with acquisition (including acqui-hire) compensation and retention design. 

- Experience with Tableau or other BI tools, or building dashboards for leaders.

- Experience scaling compensation programs through hypergrowth, IPO, or major organizational change.

- A background in a quantitative field (for example finance, statistics, engineering), or equivalent experience.

postings.description:
FEQ427R574

Senior Manager, Field Engineering Enablement – Scaled Programs and Field Capability

Databricks Field Engineering (FE) is a global organization of thousands of technical experts who help customers build on the Data Intelligence Platform, and how they learn, grow, and prove their expertise directly shapes how quickly our customers succeed. Inside FE Enablement, a strong team already runs the scaled programs that make this possible. These include communities of technical experts, programs that develop engineers into trusted advisors for customer leaders, ongoing learning that keeps experienced engineers current as the platform and AI change, and the skills standards and specialization paths that define what great looks like in the field. These programs have proven that scaled, field-led enablement works, and the opportunity now is much bigger than running them well. AI is changing what Field Engineers need to be good at, and we need a Senior Manager who can set the vision for what comes next, connect today's programs into one system that helps every engineer grow throughout their career, and design and launch the new programs the field will need. You will lead the team that built these programs and give them a clear direction and more room to build, working closely with FE leadership, product teams, the People team, and enablement partners in every region to bring that vision to life.

The impact you will have:

- Set a multi-year vision for how Field Engineers build, apply, and prove their expertise in an AI-enabled world, and turn it into a roadmap that FE leadership understands, supports, and invests in.

- Connect expert communities, trusted advisor development, ongoing learning, and skills standards into one system, so that what an engineer learns, practices, shares, and demonstrates builds on itself instead of living in separate programs with separate audiences.

- Find the next capability gaps before they slow the field down, and design and launch new scaled programs to close them, taking each from first idea to a global program that thousands of engineers use and value.

- Build a repeatable way to create programs at scale, with shared design patterns, community-led delivery, and AI built into how programs are created and run, so that launching the next program is faster and easier than the last one.

- Lead, coach, and grow the team that owns these programs, giving each person clear scope, real ownership of what they build, and a visible path to grow their careers and impact, including leading new programs as the portfolio expands.

- Give the team's work more visibility and influence with FE leadership, so that program owners have a seat where decisions about field readiness are made and their results are recognized across the organization.

- Make demonstrated capability useful to the business, working with FE leadership and the People team to connect skills and specialization to development conversations, staffing, and career growth.

- Define clear measures of adoption, proficiency, capability coverage, and impact on customer outcomes, and use that evidence to decide where to invest, what to scale, and what to retire.

What we look for:

- 10+ years of experience in technical enablement, solutions architecture or field engineering, learning and development, or program leadership at a high-growth technology company, including at least 4 years leading teams of senior individual contributors.

- A track record as a people leader who develops senior talent, gives people ownership and credit for their work, and advocates for their growth, along with references who would say they did some of their best work on your team.

- A track record of creating and launching new programs from ambiguity and scaling them to a large, global technical audience, not only running programs someone else designed.

- The ability to see how separate programs fit together, form a clear point of view on where they should go next, and bring senior leaders and your team along with that vision.

- Enough technical fluency in data and AI to earn credibility with Solutions Architects and product experts, ideally built through time in a customer-facing technical role.

- Strong strategic judgment and executive presence, with experience partnering with Directors and VPs to shape priorities, make tradeoffs, and secure investment for new work.

RDQ225R487

Job Description

Databricks is looking for a Senior Manager, Infrastructure Data Science to shape the future of Databricks infrastructure through data science. You will tackle some of the most complex challenges related to capacity planning, performance optimization, reliability engineering, infrastructure efficiency, and customer experience. You will lead a team of data scientists and work directly in partnership with engineering leaders to empower them with data-driven insights and solutions. 

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high-value challenges that are central to their missions.

Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, CA to a global organization with over 7000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in the world.

Our engineering teams build highly technical products that fulfill real, important needs in the world. We constantly push the boundaries of data and AI technology, while simultaneously operating with the resilience, security, and scale that is critical to making customers successful on our platform.

The impact you will have:

- Thought leadership and strategic guidance on infrastructure planning, balancing current needs with future growth projections to ensure scalability and cost-effectiveness.

- Promote a data-driven approach to infrastructure decisions, influencing stakeholders across engineering, and support to leverage data science insights for high-impact, aligned strategies.

- Implement data-driven solutions to identify, predict, and mitigate infrastructure risks and failures, reducing downtime and improving system reliability and performance, directly impacting end-user satisfaction and operational continuity.

- Spearhead analyses to improve resource utilization efficiency, identifying and eliminating inefficiencies across infrastructure usage, resulting in cost savings and optimized performance.

- Establish data frameworks that empower support teams to troubleshoot and resolve product issues faster, decreasing response times and enhancing customer experience and support quality.

- Mentor and manage a team of data scientists, instilling best practices in data science, engineering, and fostering a collaborative environment focused on innovative, scalable infrastructure solutions.

What we look for:

- 10+ years of infrastructure data science, machine learning, advanced analytics experience in high velocity, high-growth companies

- 5+ years of management experience hiring and developing teams

- Experience developing data science, analytics, and machine learning and AI products and capabilities in a cloud environment

- Knowledge of statistics and rigorous analytical techniques

- Experience with data visualization tools, knowledge of data engineering, data modeling, and big data technologies

Mission

As a Senior ML and AI Technical Solutions Engineer, you play a critical role by helping customers debug and maintain stable GenAI and ML Workloads with AI agent systems using the Databricks Platform. You will develop product expertise end-to-end by advising a broad set of customers and use cases across the space - including products such as Agent Bricks, Vector Search and Model Serving.
