postings.title: Specialist Solutions Architect - AI/ML (Healthcare & Life Sciences)
postings.description:
FEQ427R390

As a Specialist Solutions Architect (SSA) on the Healthcare & Life Sciences team, you will help Payers and Providers put generative AI to work at the center of their business. For Payers, that means prior authorization, claims, payment integrity, risk adjustment and the member experience. For Providers, it means clinical documentation, care management, the revenue cycle and the patient experience. Both run on complex, highly regulated data such as EHR records, claims and clinical notes. You will help them turn that data into AI on Databricks that is accurate, governed and ready for production.

In this customer-facing role, you will work with and support Solution Architects, helping customers design and implement essential workloads and shape their roadmap for expanding use of the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. As a go-to expert reporting to the Specialist Field Engineering Manager, you will keep building your skills through mentorship, learning and internal training. You will also deepen a specialty in generative AI, AI agents, Healthcare or another area.

The impact you will have

- Guide strategic Payer and Provider customers from AI prototype to production, architecting generative AI applications and agents with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), fine-tuned or open foundation models, and the data platforms behind them

- Build agents for Payer and Provider workflows such as medical coding, utilization review and member and patient service, including multi-agent systems, tool calling and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations

- Apply generative AI to clinical notes, charts, call transcripts and documents for summarization, extraction and chart review

- Ground AI in governed data through context engineering, semantic layers and natural-language analytics with Genie, so agents answer from trusted business definitions

- Set up evaluation, tracing and monitoring for AI quality, cost and latency, including LLM judges, human feedback and guardrails, using MLflow

- Build the data foundations behind AI, including batch and streaming pipelines, data warehouses and migrations from legacy platforms such as Teradata, Oracle, SQL Server, Informatica and SAS

- Bring machine learning in where it fits, such as risk, fraud and forecasting models that work alongside generative AI and agents

- Help customers work with healthcare data such as EHR, FHIR, HL7 and claims, and meet HIPAA and PHI requirements through governance with Unity Catalog

- Use AI tools, including coding assistants and agents, to move quickly from a customer problem to a working prototype and reusable solution accelerators

- Support Solution Architects on the advanced parts of the technical sale, including custom proof-of-concept content, workload sizing estimates and custom architectures

- Grow adoption of Databricks with customers and the broader community through tutorials, training, hackathons, blogs and Healthcare conference presentations

What we look for

- 5+ years of hands-on experience in a technical role, with recent hands-on work building generative AI applications or agents

- Expertise in generative AI and agents, including LLMs, RAG, agent frameworks, tool calling and MCP, prompt and context engineering, fine-tuning, evaluation and guardrails

- Experience taking AI applications or agents to production to solve business problems, including tracing, evaluation, monitoring, serving and cost control, with tools like MLflow

- A strong foundation in data engineering, data warehousing or machine learning, such as pipelines and streaming, data modeling and SQL performance, warehouse migrations, model development and MLOps

- Experience maintaining and extending production data systems as needs grow more complex

- Comfort using AI coding assistants and agents in day-to-day development and prototyping

- Production programming experience in SQL and Python, Scala or Java

- 2 years of hands-on professional experience with big data technologies (such as Spark, Hadoop and Kafka) and architectures

- 2 years of customer-facing experience in a pre-sales or post-sales role

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or Engineering, or equivalent work experience

- Ability to meet technical training and role-specific expectations within 6 months of hire

- Ability to travel up to 30% when needed

Preferred qualifications:

- Education in a healthcare-related field (for example health informatics, biostatistics, epidemiology, public health or health economics), or equivalent experience

- Experience with Payers or Providers, such as claims, care management, risk adjustment, quality measures, clinical operations, EHR data or revenue cycle management

postings.title: Specialist Solutions Architect - Data Engineering
postings.description:
(FEQ128R2)

The Role

As a Specialist Solutions Architect (SSA) – Data Engineering, you are a hands-on technical authority who guides strategic customers in designing, building, and optimizing production-grade data workloads on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. Partnering closely with Account Teams and Solution Architects, you translate complex big data challenges into high-performance, scalable architectures using Apache Spark™ and modern streaming frameworks. 

In this role, you will drive successful implementations, align technical roadmaps to accelerate platform adoption, and establish deep domain specialization; whether in real-time streaming, performance optimization, or operational data layers, while expanding your impact across Field Engineering.

The impact you will have:

- Drive Technical Wins & Scope: Lead end-to-end technical design, proof of concepts (PoCs), and workload sizing for strategic customer engagements, acting as a trusted advisor to front-line technical stakeholders to secure technical wins.

- Architect Production Data Systems: Design, build, and optimize scalable, high-performance batch and streaming pipelines, operational data layers (Lakebase), and end-to-end performance load testing on Databricks.

Sr. Automation Engineer - IT Asset Management

Req ID: GAQ427R222

About the Role

As a Senior Automation Engineer on the IT Asset Management team at Databricks, you will be the technical engine behind transforming how we manage ~$XXM/yr in asset spend across SaaS licenses and hardware. Your primary mission is to eliminate manual toil and build scalable, AI-powered automation that makes asset operations fast, accurate, and effortless as Databricks scales past 14,000 employees.

Your initial focus will be on IT asset management workflows: automating new hire laptop provisioning, SaaS license lifecycle management, asset data reconciliation, and hardware recovery. Over time, you will expand your automation footprint across IT Support and Operations, including IT support workflows, AV/VC and event support, and incident response management.

This role requires a strong automation-first mindset, the ability to learn new domains quickly, and comfort building with AI/LLM tools. You will report to the Senior Manager of IT Asset Management.

The Impact You Will Have

- New hire laptop provisioning: Build end-to-end automation for assigning, configuring, and shipping laptops to new hires, targeting a 75% reduction in manual ticket toil.

- SaaS license lifecycle: Automate license consumption monitoring, inactivity-based seat clawbacks, renewal alerting, and cost optimization workflows to help drive $1.5M+ in annual savings and cost avoidance.

- Asset data quality: Automate CMDB/inventory reconciliation, deduplication, and multi-device detection to bring asset records to audit-ready accuracy.

- Offboarding asset recovery: Automate tracking and recovery of hardware from exiting employees, reducing loss and improving chain-of-custody compliance.

- Broader IT Ops automation (over time): Extend automation into IT support, AV/VC and event support, and incident response management as the ITAM automation foundation matures.

What We Are Looking For

Core Qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in IT systems engineering, automation engineering, or a related technical role.

- Proven track record of delivering complex, multi-system automation projects with measurable business impact.

- Strong automation-first mindset: you see a manual process and immediately think about how to build a scalable, reliable automated solution.

- Ability to operate with minimal guidance, take ownership of ambiguous problems, and deliver consistently high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.

- We value a great generalist who can learn a domain quickly over a narrow specialist. You should be comfortable ramping into unfamiliar systems and business processes and building effective automation without needing deep prior domain expertise.

AI and LLM Automation

- Hands-on experience building workflows, agents, or tools powered by large language models (e.g., Claude, GPT, Gemini, or similar).

- Ability to design AI-powered automation that handles unstructured inputs, makes decisions, and integrates with enterprise systems.

- Experience with prompt engineering, agent frameworks, or AI-assisted code generation in a production or operational context.

- Comfort evaluating and selecting the right AI approach for a given problem, whether that is a deterministic rule, an LLM call, or a hybrid.

Automation and Integration

- Experience building and troubleshooting integrations between IT platforms such as ITSM tools (FreshService, ServiceNow, or similar), identity platforms, and asset management systems.

- Experience designing automation for IT operational processes: onboarding/offboarding, access provisioning, license management, asset tracking, or similar.

- Familiarity with REST APIs, scripting (Python, Bash, or similar), and the ability to connect systems that were not designed to talk to each other.

- Experience with data pipelines, ETL, or data quality workflows is a plus.

Collaboration and Communication

- Strong cross-functional collaboration skills. Comfortable working with IT operations, security, procurement, finance, and vendor partners.

- Effective at documenting solutions and training peers on new tools and processes.

- Clear communicator who can translate complex technical work into business terms for non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to Have

- Experience with Databricks, data lakehouse architectures, or SQL-based analytics platforms.

- Experience with IT asset management or SaaS management tools (e.g., Oomnitza, Productiv, Zluri, or similar).

- Experience with no-code/low-code automation platforms (e.g., Tines, Workato, or similar).

postings.title: Sr Compensation Manager, International
postings.description:
GAQ327R301

Mission

Databricks is looking for a strategic compensation leader who likes to build. As the first dedicated international member of the Compensation team, you'll be a trusted partner to founders, senior leaders, People Partners, Recruiting, and the broader Compensation team, supporting our expanding EMEA and APJ regions. You'll create compensation solutions that help us attract, retain and motivate world-class talent, and you'll use AI to build the tools that make those solutions scale. This role reports to the Director of Compensation.

At Databricks, compensation is more than a number. It's how we show that every employee is an owner and part of our success. We're looking for someone with a strong foundation and a track record of doing exactly that.

Databricks is a deeply technical, fast-moving company, with a global footprint. You'll partner with dynamic, data-driven leaders who value rigorous analysis, clear perspectives, and collaborative problem-solving. In this role, priorities can evolve quickly, and you'll often navigate multiple important initiatives at once.

We set high standards for this role to support our fast-paced growth. Successful team members in this environment tend to:

- Build trust through analytical rigor. You present well-reasoned models and effectively articulate complex analysis to engineering leaders who will test your assumptions.

- Navigate fast-paced priorities with resilience. You maintain focus, sound judgment, and positivity when balancing competing deadlines and feedback.

- Offer constructive perspectives. You confidently partner with senior stakeholders to propose data-backed alternative solutions and drive alignment to finalize decisions.

- Embrace feedback as a growth tool. You extract actionable insights from feedback and respond with clarity and openness.

- Create order from ambiguity. When there's no playbook, you build one, and you're comfortable acting on 80% of the information.

If you are excited by high standards, technical depth, and collaborative strategic discussions, you will find this work deeply rewarding.

The impact you will have

This is a hands-on, high-impact role. Expected time on each area:

International compensation solutions and strategic advice (40%)

- Help evolve Databricks’ international compensation strategy as we scale, including our approach to geographic differentiation, market positioning, salary structures, and equity, while working directly with international leaders to diagnose talent challenges and design attraction and retention solutions.

- Partner closely with HR teams and business executives across global divisions to translate US compensation practices internationally, offering localized strategies, pay equity assessments (including EU pay transparency compliance), key talent retention initiatives, and macro-level guidance as Databricks enters and scales in new markets.

- Serve as the main compensation advisor on strategic hires and high-stakes retention situations for niche international talent.

- Turn vague or urgent requests into clear options with explicit tradeoffs, then help leaders reach a decision.

- Regularly coordinate and partner with US-based Compensation Partners to ensure seamless continuity of support for business leaders in a globally matrixed setup.

AI-enabled lifecycle compensation (30%)

- Run merit, refresh equity and promotion cycles for global teams.

- Design and build AI tools and workflows that reduce manual work and improve decisions. Examples include offer modeling, retention-risk analysis, cycle quality checks, and self-serve insights for leaders.

- Spot what's repetitive or error-prone in today's processes and automate it.

Enterprise compensation frameworks (30%)

- Spearhead ongoing and upcoming strategic rewards initiatives, helping build the infrastructure, principles, and enablement that will allow Databricks' international compensation framework to scale alongside job architecture, market pricing models, pay-for-performance design, and equity strategy.

- Build frameworks that solve today's problems and anticipate the ones coming as we grow.

- Partner with the Compensation Programs team as they lead, manage, and support enterprise-wide programs, collaborating closely on international considerations and matters.

What we look for

Quantitative and technical skill is the foundation of this role. Everything else we look for builds on it.

1. Compensation expertise

- You know your craft. Job architecture, compensation frameworks, market pricing, year-end and mid-year pay cycles, global compensation practices, and pay-for-performance design.

- You know the competition. Deep knowledge of competitor compensation, especially new-hire and refresh equity strategy at high-growth and public tech companies with global footprints. 

- You know the market. You formulate and conduct detailed benchmarking studies to monitor market movements, bridge data deficits, and offer validated recommendations to the business.

- You reason from first principles. You balance compensation best practice with what the business actually needs, and you can rebuild a framework from its underlying logic when the standard approach doesn't fit.

2. Quantitative and technical foundation

- Expert-level analytical modeling. You build compensation models from scratch, including cost-of-program scenarios, pay-positioning analysis, attrition and retention-risk modeling, and sensitivity and tradeoff analysis. 

- Built with AI. You've personally used AI tools (for example LLMs, AI assistants, or automation and agent platforms) to build compensation tools, models or workflows that others rely on. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to explain how it works, what you'd improve, and how you checked that its outputs were accurate.

- Equity fluency. You bring deep equity expertise to translate Databricks' equity philosophy across markets where candidate expectations and familiarity with US-style equity compensation vary significantly, grounded in a solid understanding of RSU and option mechanics, vesting design, and refresh strategy.

- Statistical judgment. You know when a market data cut is credible, when a sample is too small, and how to present ranges and market pricing without false precision.

3. Strategic partnership

- Trusted advisor to senior leaders. You have a track record of advising executives on sensitive, high-stakes compensation decisions (offers, promotions, leveling, retention, transfers, org changes) and influencing the outcome through data and judgment rather than authority.

- Operational excellence. You connect the dots between systems, stakeholders and programs to deliver compensation programs end to end, accurately and on time.

- Clear communicator. You turn complex analysis into a crisp recommendation an executive can act on in one conversation.

About the Role

Databricks is looking for an experienced commercial attorney to join our Commercial Legal team, with a primary focus on supporting our Healthcare and Life Sciences (HLS) sales teams.

Our HLS customers - health systems, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, medical device and diagnostics companies, payers and health services companies, healthcare technology and data companies, and clinical research organizations - bring some of the most complex and interesting legal work on the commercial team. The customers on the other side of the table are sophisticated and heavily regulated, with specific compliance, privacy, and security requirements that need to be understood and addressed. 

You'll work side-by-side with Sales to lead negotiations, shape deal strategy, and address the issues that matter most to regulated customers - from HIPAA and data privacy to AI terms and security requirements. The role requires strong commercial judgment, the ability to build trust with sales teams and customers alike, and a practical approach to risk. You'll also have a front-row seat to how AI is transforming legal work. Our team is actively building and using AI-powered tools for contract review, research, drafting, and knowledge management, and you'll be part of shaping what that looks like. This position reports to the Senior Director & Associate General Counsel, Commercial.

The impact you will have:

- Lead complex commercial transactions from first engagement through signature, including drafting and negotiating SaaS MSAs and related security and privacy terms, as well as order forms, statements of work, and related transaction documents

- Negotiate healthcare-specific agreements and provisions, including business associate agreements, healthcare data privacy and security terms, and regulatory compliance requirements

- Partner closely with Sales, Deal Desk, Finance, Security, Privacy, Product, and other stakeholders to resolve issues that affect deal execution

- Advise on issues that arise in enterprise technology transactions with regulated customers, including data privacy, information security, artificial intelligence, intellectual property, open source software, and healthcare-specific regulatory requirements

- Help improve templates, playbooks, fallback positions, guidance, and contracting processes - including building institutional knowledge on HLS-specific deal patterns

- Leverage AI tools to work more efficiently and contribute to the team's adoption of AI-assisted legal workflows

- Provide concise, practical legal advice that balances legal risk with commercial objectives

What we look for:

- 7+ years of relevant technology transactions experience at a law firm and/or in-house legal department

- Significant experience drafting, negotiating, and closing complex sell-side software, SaaS, and cloud transactions with enterprise customers

- Experience supporting customers in healthcare, life sciences, or other heavily regulated industries, with a working knowledge of HIPAA and experience negotiating or advising on business associate agreements and healthcare data privacy requirements

- Strong familiarity with issues that commonly arise in commercial technology deals, including data privacy, information security, intellectual property, and open source software

- Experience advising on AI-related contract terms, data use provisions, and emerging technology issues in enterprise transactions, and a demonstrated interest in using AI tools to improve the efficiency and quality of legal work

- Demonstrated ability to independently manage sophisticated negotiations, exercise sound judgment, and translate legal and business risk into practical advice

- Strong communication and prioritization skills, and the ability to manage multiple matters effectively

What we look for:

The Senior Counsel, Employment will provide sophisticated, practical legal advice to the Databricks People Team and business leaders, with a particular focus on HR AI adoption, compensation and benefits, pay equity, global mobility, employee privacy, and M&A (diligence, employee-related deal terms, and workforce integration). This person will be based in the U.S. and advise directly on U.S. matters, but will also lead and project-manage complex global projects. Regular cross-functional partners will include recruiting, privacy and product legal, security, tax, people operations, comp and benefits, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will be a pragmatic and resourceful advisor and an enthusiastic AI user, with strong project-management discipline and the ability to move quickly while maintaining a high standard of legal and operational precision. In addition to the focus areas above, this person will collaborate to resolve U.S. disputes.

This is a full-time position reporting to Databricks' Senior Director and Associate General Counsel of Global Employment Legal and working closely with a team of employment lawyers and legal professionals across multiple regions.

Responsibilities

- Advise on cash compensation programs, bonus and incentive plans, clawback policies, equal-pay requirements, pay equity reviews, compensation governance, and related internal and external disclosures. Lead or support pay equity projects, including scoping, data and process review, coordination with stakeholders, review of analyses, and development of remediation or communication plans.

- Provide legal advice on employee benefits, including retirement plans, welfare and wrap plans, severance plans, leave-related benefits, and country-specific benefits and protections, partnering with benefits counsel and regional employment legal team members as appropriate.

- Draft, review, and update employment-related plans, policies, agreements, templates, and employee communications with exceptional precision and attention to detail.

- Advise recruiting and talent acquisition teams on candidate-facing issues, offer letters, employment agreements, compensation terms, background checks, hiring practices, and negotiations, often on time-sensitive matters.

- Advise on global mobility and immigration matters, including employee transfers, international assignments, work authorization, permanent residence processes, employer-of-record and professional-employer-organization arrangements, cross-border moves, and related onboarding or exit issues.

- Support the employment-related aspects of mergers, acquisitions, and strategic investments, including employment and benefits diligence, workforce mapping, employee-related deal terms, retention and vesting arrangements, transition and separation arrangements, and post-closing workforce integration.

- Advise on employee privacy and data-use issues, including employee and candidate data, access and disclosure requests, workforce technology, monitoring, data transfers, and the employment implications of business and HR systems.

- Review and advise on HR AI tools and workflows, including vendor diligence, recruiting, use-case design, employment-law and privacy risks, bias and discrimination considerations, governance controls, documentation, and responsible implementation.

- Lead global employment-related projects, including international expansions, from scoping through implementation, including developing workplans, identifying stakeholders and dependencies, coordinating regional counsel and outside advisors, managing timelines and budgets, documenting decisions, and driving issues to resolution.

- Monitor legal developments affecting compensation, benefits, pay equity, recruiting, mobility, privacy, AI, and other relevant employment areas, and translate those developments into practical guidance, process changes, and training for internal clients.

- Identify and implement process improvements that help the Legal and People Teams scale, including playbooks, decision frameworks, repeatable workflows, knowledge-management practices, and automated or AI-enabled solutions.

- Serve as a hands-on problem solver for sensitive, high-priority, and cross-functional issues, exercising sound judgment about when to escalate matters to legal leadership or engage specialized counsel.

- Respond to U.S. demand letters, administrative charges, and other disputes, including investigating claims, communicating with opposing counsel, negotiating resolutions, and drafting separation and settlement agreements.

- JD from a top-tier law school; member of a state bar in good standing.

- 10+ years of relevant employment-law experience, with substantial experience advising sophisticated organizations; in-house experience, including firm secondee experience, strongly preferred.

- Experience with compensation, benefits, pay equity, executive compensation, recruiting, global mobility, and immigration.

- Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and strategic investments, including employment and benefits diligence, employee-related deal terms, and workforce integration.

- Experience leading multi-jurisdictional or global projects and coordinating stakeholders across regions, functions, and levels of seniority.

- Experience advising on employee privacy, workforce data, HR technology, and AI tools is strongly preferred.

- Exceptional drafting skills, including the ability to produce precise, clear, audience-appropriate agreements, policies, memoranda, guidance, and executive communications.

- Strong project-management skills, including the ability to define scope, create structure from ambiguity, manage dependencies, maintain momentum, and deliver high-quality work on deadline.

- Ability to quickly and independently assess unfamiliar or time-sensitive situations, identify the material risks, and develop practical options to resolve them.

- Ability to build strong relationships quickly and work effectively with executive stakeholders.

- Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, high-growth technology company and to make progress with incomplete information.

- Genuine enthusiasm for AI and emerging technology.

Databricks is at the forefront of data and AI innovation, and our Legal team plays a vital role in supporting this mission. We are dedicated to navigating complex legal landscapes and ensuring compliance within the rapidly evolving technology sector. Our team is composed of diverse legal professionals with expertise in technology, privacy, intellectual property, corporate law, cybersecurity, employment law, tax, regulatory compliance, and litigation.

About the Role

Databricks is seeking a talented and experienced Senior Counsel, Privacy to serve as a trusted advisor across the business. In this role you will own and mature our privacy program, lead legal initiatives that deliver cutting-edge, practical legal advice as we navigate rapidly evolving global privacy and AI laws. Reporting to the Director & Assistant General Counsel, Privacy, you will develop AI-enabled solutions for operating and maturing the privacy processes and controls that keep Databricks compliant.

You will be agile and highly organized, with the skills, drive, and flexibility to build and scale a program at a leading technology company, addressing cutting-edge legal issues and organizational challenges. A successful candidate will be an AI proficient builder, resourceful self-starter, comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, and excellent at building strong relationships and driving cross-functional execution.

The impact you will have

- Legal advice and regulatory interpretation. Advise on compliance with global privacy and data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, ADMT, and other U.S. state laws, Monitor legal and regulatory developments, and translate them into actionable guidance for the business. 

- Privacy Program & Governance Leadership: Build and mature Databricks’ privacy program to continue meeting evolving regulatory expectations, including contributions to AI governance. Develop core program components for compliance with new regulations, including data subject rights requests, privacy notices, consent management, PIA/DPIAs, and policy management.

- Risk assessments. Conduct gap analysis and risk assessments, including Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), and transfer impact assessments to identify, assess, and help mitigate privacy risk, and support the organization's records of processing activities (RoPA).

- Contract Negotiation and Transactions: Draft and update form agreements, and counsel on and negotiate data protection provisions in commercial contracts, including data processing addendums (DPAs), standard contractual clauses (SCCs), and related data-transfer instruments.

- Policies, training, and governance. Develop and maintain internal privacy policies, external privacy notices, and standards. Design and deliver privacy training and awareness programs, and help operationalize privacy and AI governance frameworks and cross-functional privacy committees.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration & Legal Partnership: Build deep cross-functional relationships and collaborate with other legal leaders in commercial, go-to-market, compliance, corporate, and public affairs on privacy issues.

- Business and Legal Judgment: Exercise practical judgment about when to approve, approve with conditions, decline, or escalate.

- Team Contribution: Provide general legal support on a flexible, as-needed basis across other areas of the business, and contribute as a team player to further the legal department's reputation as an effective, respected, and valued resource within the company.

What we look for

- 7+ years of relevant legal experience at a top law firm and/or in-house (a combination of both is a plus), with 5+ years focused on privacy and demonstrated experience building, operating, or leading a privacy compliance program (not solely advisory work)

- Deep, current knowledge of global privacy and AI frameworks, including the GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, EU AI Act, and the growing patchwork of U.S. state comprehensive privacy and AI laws, and familiarity with cross-border data transfer mechanisms (SCCs, IDTA, adequacy, EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework). 

- Working knowledge of the operational building blocks of a privacy program — DPIAs/PIAs, ROPA and data mapping, data subject rights processes, privacy by design, and vendor/third-party risk management

- Technical proficiency in using AI tools to build skills, agents, and other automated tasks.

- Capacity to be a generalist and learn new areas of law and legal skills quickly as the business evolves

- Deep understanding of cloud and software technology, and a strong desire to work on legal issues in these areas

- Experience working for a company offering platform services to business customers is a plus

- Familiarity with privacy management tooling (e.g., OneTrust or comparable) is a plus

- J.D. from a top-tier law school

- State bar membership required, in good standing

- One or more privacy certifications (e.g., CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM, CIPT, FIP) preferred; CIPM is particularly valued for a program-leadership role

What you bring

- You can set the direction for a program and drive it into execution — prioritizing and managing time and client expectations amid competing demands, often without direct guidance, as we scale our rapidly expanding business.

- You exercise good judgment in raising issues, assessing risk, and providing concise, actionable, business-focused legal advice and counsel.

- You build strong, deep working relationships with internal stakeholders across multiple geographies and functions, and are comfortable working with distributed teams.

- You are a self-starter who operates independently and interacts confidently with senior management, influencing without authority.

- You have a strong work ethic, excellent organizational skills, and the ability to manage many cross-functional projects simultaneously with minimal supervision.

- You have outstanding written and verbal communication skills and can make complex privacy and regulatory concepts clear to both legal and non-legal audiences, including executives.

postings.title: Sr. Deployment Strategist
postings.description:
CSQ128R189

As a Deployment Strategist (FDS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the entire non-technical lifecycle of an FDE engagement.

You will partner with our Account Executives to build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and, most importantly, scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing.

This role requires a rare mix of C-suite gravitas, deep product-style thinking, and a hands-on, get it done execution mindset.

You will report to the Director, Forward Deployed Engineering.

The impact you will have:

- C-Suite Scoping & Value Definition: Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value ($10M+ problems), and define the pilot (MVP, success criteria, timeline).

- End-to-End Product Ownership: Act as the CEO of the project by authoring the PRD, prioritizing the engineering backlog, relentlessly managing scope, and acting as the primary hands-on QA tester.

- Agile Project Execution & Delivery: Drive the FDE build team via an agile process, manage all stakeholder communications from the C-suite to individual engineers, and act as the escalation manager to unblock all technical or political issues.

- Solution Launch & Landing: Own the Day 0 launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value.

- Strategic Handoff & Growth: Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement.

What we look for:

- Executive Presence & Communication: A Trusted Advisor with C-suite gravitas and superb communication skills. You are opinionated, humble, and can build rapport and drive decisions in days, not weeks.

- Product & Strategy Mindset: A Product Thinker and Systems Thinker who can perform a SWOT analysis, understand a competitive landscape, and define what to build and why.

- Relentless Execution: An Execution Driver with a Hands-On mentality. You are relentless, an expert at escalation, and willing to do the unglamorous work to get the project done.

- Ideal Experience: 2+ years as a Deployment Strategist OR 2+ years at a high-growth startup in a builder or founder capacity. (Alternatively: 5+ years in a senior, client-facing product or delivery role at a top-tier tech company or consultancy).

- Proven Skills: Demonstrated experience in value-based scoping (TCO/ROI), managing agile software projects, writing PRDs, and the ability/interest to travel up to 50%.

postings.title: Sr. Designated Support Engineer
postings.description:
P-1448

Important Notes: 

- This is a hybrid role and requires ~3 days in the office in São Paulo-SP. Our office is in Av Faria Lima.

- Please, submit your application and resume in English.

About the Role

As a Designated Support Engineer (DSE) at Databricks, you will serve as the principal technical support advisor and voice of the customer for our most strategic enterprise accounts leveraging technical experience and business skills.

In this role, you will lead high-touch, support-driven customer engagements, and provide proactive advisory. You will leverage support trends, ticket history, and operational telemetry to ensure the operational health, scale, and resiliency of customer data platforms. This self-motivated professional will demonstrate high commitment to both customers and internal teams, with excellent communication, project management, and problem-solving skills.

While this is a support-anchored role, you will play a critical role in driving proactive operational best practices, mitigating risk, and bridging customer challenges directly with Databricks Product, Engineering, and Field teams.

Responsibilities & Core Duties

- Technical & Architectural Guidance: Guide external stakeholders on operational best practices and architectural design across Distributed Data Processing (Apache Spark™), Query Optimization, Lakehouse open table formats (Delta Lake, Iceberg), Cloud Infrastructure & IaC, OS, Networking and Containerization (Kubernetes/Docker), Security & Governance, and Data Warehousing.

- Proactive Operational Health & Trend Analysis: Leverage support history, ticket metrics, and system telemetry to deliver predictive health checks, risk assessments, and preventive recommendations - applying deep platform domain knowledge to advise customers on environment scaling, upgrade readiness, and long-term platform stability.

- Critical Escalation & Technical Incident Facilitation: Coordinate and facilitate critical, high-impact escalations by aligning customer leadership with internal Databricks Escalation Engineers and Core Engineering teams to ensure swift, well-communicated resolutions.

- Strategic Support Ownership: Serve as the strategic ambassador for the Databricks Support organization, operating as the customer’s dedicated operational quarterback to align platform operations with business goals and ensure enterprise accounts realize maximum business value.

- Executive Reporting & Operational Governance: Lead regular Support Business Reviews (SBRs/QBRs) for customer leadership, articulating ticket health trends, Root Cause Analyses (RCAs), upgrade readiness roadmaps, and strategic operational trade-offs.

- Voice of the Customer Advocacy: Synthesize customer operational patterns, systemic technical friction, and platform blockers, channeling actionable feedback directly into Databricks Product, Support, and Engineering organizations to steer platform reliability and enhance customer experience.

Basic Qualifications:

- 5+ years of experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Premier Support Engineer (DSE), Technical Account Manager (TAM), Solutions Architect, or Senior Escalation Engineer in distributed data or cloud environments.

- Minimum 3 years’ experience designing, developing, testing, and sustaining Python, Java, or Scala-based applications.

- Demonstrated technical depth in three (3) or more of the following core domains:

- Distributed Data & Lakehouse Architectures: Apache Spark™, Delta Lake, structured streaming, and query execution/tuning.

- Cloud Infrastructure & Automation: AWS, Azure, or GCP compute/storage/networking and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform).

- OS, Networking & Containerization: Linux administration, core networking protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S), and container orchestration (Docker/Kubernetes).

- Security & Data Governance: Enterprise IAM, SSO/OAuth, network security, and data governance frameworks (e.g., Databricks Unity Catalog).

- Data Warehousing & Analytics: OLAP query plan optimization, indexing, and data platform performance tuning.

- Support Telemetry & Trend Analysis: Proven ability to leverage case data, ticket telemetry, and root-cause analyses (RCAs) to identify patterns, mitigate operational risks, and drive case/escalation reduction goals.

- Customer Leadership Influence: Track record of advising and influencing customer technical leaders (Managers, Directors, Lead Architects) on operationalizing, scaling, and optimizing platform environments.

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, STEM field, or equivalent practical experience.

postings.description:
RDQ327R182

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's most challenging problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating medical breakthroughs. Are you a Developer Advocate who thrives in the spotlight, loves presenting and hosting events, and is genuinely hands-on with agentic developer tooling — the kind of person who has already wired up three coding agents and has opinions about what breaks?

As a Senior Developer Advocate for Omnigent, you'll be a vital bridge between our engineering teams and the open source community forming around Omnigent, our meta-harness for AI agents. Omnigent sits one level above harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Pi, giving developers a common interface to compose agents, govern them with contextual policies, sandboxing, and cost controls, and collaborate on live sessions from any device. Your focus is squarely on the open source project and the community around it: templates, demos, and reference implementations that developers can clone, fork, and extend, and the contributors who will help the project grow beyond us.

The Engagement Manager is responsible for helping customers accelerate value through the adoption of the Databricks platform working with them defining and orchestrating the required engagement to ensure success.

As an Engagement Manager, you will ensure that our customers are making the most value of our products and services by positioning, preparing, managing the delivery and follow-up of our professional services and training engagements. This role is a strategic and cross-functional position that will partner closely with Sales, Field Engineering, Partners Support and Product Teams on campaigns, programs, and content. You will report to the Sr. Director, Professional Services

The impact you will have:

- Demonstrate a passion for the job and lead by example by putting Databricks and our customers first to achieve the sales and delivery mission

- Collaborate with the sales counterpart and engages early in the sales process to seek to understand our customer's needs, their business, how success is defined, and ensure that we are exceeding expectations in delivery and developing valued solutions

- Identify opportunities for new services by understanding and addressing potential new use-cases and the ability to articulate the business value in the upsell, or extension of services

- Develop commercial models including leveraging Databricks and Partner investment vehicles to help address our customer budgetary constraints for success.

- Performs as the Engagement Manager in the assigned area with full accountability for meeting/exceeding Professional Services and Training KPIs.

- Ability to articulate relevant customer success stories, services offerings, and metrics that demonstrate value to the customer

- Consult with clients to understand and analyze engagement scope, requirements, time, cost and benefits. Responsible for estimating, scoping and developing the statement of work documents as necessary

- Drive resolution of delivery challenges, address resource contentions, scoping issues and manage expectations

- Data and AI domain knowledge and experience working with customers to realise business value through to production implementations

- Proven experience in senior customer-facing roles that require a mix of influencing, validating, negotiating, understanding and execution

- Excellent customer-facing skills and the ability to communicate with and develop strong relationships at all levels including with senior executives both internally and externally

- Consistent track record of identifying customer needs and successfully implementing solutions

- Demonstrate strong leadership experience, the ability to enforce good project governance and drive delivery excellence

- Strong service delivery and program management skills with the ability to synthesize customer success outcomes into well-structured program plans that deliver against such outcomes

- Proven experience in estimating effort and scope for services 

- Proven experience in meeting and achieving KPI and targets including CSAT, Bookings and Revenue.

- Outstanding communication and customer relationship skills

postings.description:
CSQ327R208

At Databricks, our core principles are at the heart of everything we do; creating a culture of proactiveness and a customer-centric mindset guides us to create a unified platform that makes data science and analytics accessible to everyone. We aim to inspire our customers to make informed decisions that push their business forward. We provide a user-friendly and intuitive platform that makes it easy to turn insights into action and fosters a culture of creativity, experimentation, and continuous improvement. You will be an essential part of this mission, using your technical expertise to demonstrate how our Data Intelligence Platform can help customers solve their complex data challenges. You'll work with a collaborative, customer-focused team that values innovation and creativity, using your skills to create customized solutions to help our customers achieve their goals and guide their businesses forward. Join us in our quest to change how people work with data and make a better world!

As a Sr. Field Technical Program Manager at Databricks, you will be a key driver in our Forward Deployed Engineering team's mission to accelerate and de-risk customer outcomes. Your role is central to achieving project goals and maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction, particularly within our Healthcare & Life Sciences customer base. While you are not expected to have hands-on coding experience, your technical acumen and strategic influence will be critical for guiding complex engagements to success. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver excellence at every stage.

The impact you will have:

- Be responsible for the successful delivery of our most complex customer engagements by providing technical leadership and guidance to the implementation team.

- Guide technical teams through key architectural decisions, helping them navigate trade-offs between established and innovative approaches.

- Proactively identify and mitigate technical risks and dependencies that could impact project timelines and goals.

- Individually deliver on commitments by producing high-quality deliverables, status reports, program plans, and customer responses that require minimal rework.

- Effectively manage all aspects of a program, including scope, schedule, budget, risk, and resources, with a focus on technical complexity.

- Act as the primary point of escalation for customers regarding technical delivery issues and, as needed, escalate to other parts of Databricks for rapid resolution.

- Build trust and credibility with technical teams and stakeholders by clearly articulating Databricks’ vision and solutions and facilitating productive, goal-oriented meetings.

What we look for:

- Technical Acumen & Decision Making: A proven ability to stay current on technology trends and make sound technical decisions without being a hands-on coder.

- Program & Project Management: Experience managing large, complex engagements and mitigating unexpected technical challenges. Familiarity with managing the trade-offs between scope, budget, and timeline.

- Communication & Leadership: Excellent communication, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills. A track record of influencing technical teams and effectively tailoring messages for different audiences, from engineers to executives.

- Experience with BI, data management, and big data technologies is preferred.

- Proven ability to multitask and manage multiple engagements while delivering a high level of customer satisfaction.

postings.title: Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer
postings.description:
CSQ427R94

As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) you will work with customers to build and productionize solutions to their data & AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You will own the architecture, lead design decisions, and implement end-to-end systems spanning data engineering, AI, and application development. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations. FDEs deliver with customer empathy, integrating with client systems, training, and other technical needs to help customers get most value out of their data. 

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for builders who thrive at the intersection of technology and business impact. The ideal candidate combines engineering expertise with adaptability, curiosity, and a passion for working with customers and teammates to solve complex problems that drive measurable outcomes. FDEs are billable and know how to complete projects according to specification with exceptional customer empathy.

The impact you will have:

- Production Solution Delivery: Lead impactful customer technical projects by delivering production-grade systems, designing and building reference architectures, custom applications and data ingestion and ML/AI model integration

- Transformational Impact: Guide strategic customers as they implement transformational big data projects including end-to-end design, build and deployment of industry-leading big data and AI applications. Work with engagement managers to scope technical delivery work with input from the customer

- Empower Customers: Guide customers on architecture and design; bootstrap or implement customer projects which leads to a customers' successful understanding, evaluation and adoption of Databricks.

- Own the Architecture: Lead architecture and design decisions, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, and aligned with both customer needs and Databricks best practices.

- Work with the Databricks technical team, Project Manager, Architect and Customer team to ensure the technical components of the engagement are delivered to meet customer's needs.

- Work with Engineering and Databricks Customer Support to provide product and implementation feedback and to guide rapid resolution for engagement specific product and support issues.

- Customer Immersion: Embed with customer teams, engaging with stakeholders from technical ICs to executives to deeply understand challenges and deliver impact.

- Reusable Assets & Scale: Contribute accelerators, frameworks, and best practices that scale impact across accounts and influence the Databricks product roadmap.

What we look for:

- 6+ years experience in data engineering, data platforms & analytics, or software engineering

- Comfortable writing code in either Python, Scala, JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern frameworks

- Working knowledge of two or more common Cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP) with expertise in at least one

- Deep experience with distributed computing with Apache Spark™ and knowledge of Spark runtime internals

- Familiarity with CI/CD for production deployments

- Working knowledge of MLOps, ML/AI models and AI APIs

- Design and deployment of performant production end-to-end data architectures and applications that combine data pipelines, ML/AI models, and user-facing interfaces.

- Experience with technical project delivery - managing scope, timelines and measurable outcomes, translating complex concepts into actionable solutions.

- Documentation and white-boarding skills.

- Experience working with enterprise clients and managing conflicts across a broad stakeholder range

- Build skills in technical areas, and demonstrate curiosity, adaptability, and eagerness to explore new technologies which support the deployment and integration of Databricks-based solutions to complete customer projects.

- Travel to customers 20% of the time

RDQ427R365

At Databricks, we are passionate about helping data teams solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

We are the “AI/BI” Dashboard team responsible for making Databricks the best product for business users to create, share and consume data insights. We own the entire product stack end-2-end: the Dashboard creation and consumption UI, the query and permissions layer, the control plane for the service, the consumption surface across web, mobile and Desktop as well as the distribution infrastructure across various channels (e-Mail, Mobile, Slack/Teams etc.). At every layer of our stack, we are leveraging AI to change how users interact with and leverage our product in completely new ways to find the answers they need quicker than ever before. 

We're seeking a dedicated Senior Engineering Manager who will help grow the AI/BI Dashboard product and service platform. This means tackling a number of challenging fullstack and backend problem spaces, for example making agentic dashboard authoring and AI insights fast and performant while maintaining high quality, enabling the creation and consumption of Dashboards and BI features across the entire Databricks platform and scaling our service to the next order of magnitude of users. This role also requires experience in applying AI and LLM technology directly into the product surface and guiding the team to strike a balance between pushing up quality while maintaining performance and cost. 

You will report directly to the Director of Engineering.

The main responsibilities include:

- You will lead multiple talented engineering teams of full stack/backend engineers and SMEs as well as managers focused on the above initiatives.

- You will oversee sustained recruitment of top-tier IC talent and Managers, and developing talent across the teams.

- You will build processes to implement product vision and strategy, according to organizational goals and priorities.

- You will build software that is not just high quality, but easy to operate.

What we look for:

- Great at hiring and developing talent

postings.title: Sr. Manager, Security — Continuous Monitoring v 2.0
postings.description:
RDQ227R1175

While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations will be considered.

About Databricks

Databricks is the data and AI company. More than 12,000 organizations worldwide — including Comcast, Condé Nast, Grammarly, and over 50% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to unify and democratize data, analytics and AI.

Databricks is headquartered in San Francisco, with offices around the globe and was founded by the original creators of Lakehouse, Apache Spark™, Delta Lake and MLflow.

About the Team

The Continuous Monitoring (ConMon) team at Databricks builds and operates the engineering infrastructure that keeps Databricks' security control posture visible, measurable, and defensible at all times.

We build automation that continuously assesses whether security controls are actually working across cloud environments, SaaS platforms, identity systems, and enterprise applications — surfacing drift, coverage gaps, and control failures as they happen rather than at the next audit.

Our work sits at the intersection of security engineering and GRC: we turn control requirements into code, evidence collection into automation, and security posture into intelligence that drives decisions.

The ConMon team also maintains security tooling and scanning infrastructure to aid control evaluation. This includes scanning for secret leaks, asset vulnerabilities, and SAST.

As Databricks' security program, cloud footprint, and regulatory obligations all scale, the Continuous Monitoring team is responsible for ensuring the company's control posture is always verifiable, always current, and never a surprise.

The Role

Databricks is looking for a Senior Manager to lead the Continuous Monitoring team.

You will own the engineering function that measures whether Databricks' security controls are working — across cloud infrastructure, identity, SaaS, and enterprise systems — and turns that measurement into something the Security organization, and its auditors, can rely on.

That includes demonstrating control posture against the frameworks the business carries (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, and emerging AI governance requirements), but the underlying question is broader: are the controls Databricks depends on actually in place and operating everywhere they are supposed to be?

This is an engineering management role. The team writes production Python, operates data pipelines against cloud and SaaS APIs, and integrates with GRC and security tooling. Success is measured in control coverage, the accuracy and timeliness of what the team reports, and how quickly gaps get to the people who can close them.

The role requires enough technical depth to review that work credibly, and enough judgement to prioritize the controls where measurement actually reduces risk.

As the leader of Continuous Monitoring, you'll be responsible for growing and developing the team; setting a clear vision, priority, and strategy; making the case for the headcount and tooling the program needs; and building durable partnerships across GRC (SAC, SAF, Governance, Risk Management, TPRM), IT, Legal, and Engineering — the organizations that own the controls your team monitors.

The Impact You Will Have

Team Building & People Leadership

- Hire strong Security Software Engineers who bring genuine engineering skill to compliance automation.

- Support engineers in their career development with clear, specific feedback; develop senior ICs into technical leaders and grow the next generation of security engineering managers.

- Set and hold a high bar for engineering quality: code review standards, reliability and observability expectations for automation pipelines, and documentation that remains useful across audit cycles and team changes.

- Build a team that combines GRC domain knowledge with software engineering discipline, and hire for both.

Control Measurement Program Ownership

- Own the strategy and roadmap for Databricks' continuous monitoring platform — control state collection at cloud scale, continuous posture assessment, security and GRC tooling integration, and remediation tracking.

- Define what the program measures and why: prioritize the controls whose failure would matter most to Databricks' security posture, rather than defaulting to the set a given framework happens to enumerate.

- Ensure coverage keeps pace with the business — new cloud environments, new products and services, new certifications and regulatory obligations, and AI governance controls that current tooling does not yet assess.

- Reduce manual evidence collection systematically; set and track targets for automated control coverage, freshness, and audit burden on Engineering teams.

- Own the accuracy of the team's output, including false positive rates; findings should be reliable enough that control owners act on them without re-verification.

Posture Visibility & Executive Intelligence

- Own the security posture dashboards, metrics, and reporting that give Security and GRC leadership an accurate, timely view of control health across the company.

- Define the metrics the program reports on — control coverage, drift, time-to-remediate, and where the organization is exposed — and build the reporting that leadership uses to make security investment and prioritization decisions.

- Present the team's findings to senior leadership: control gaps and drift, their risk implications, and the effort required to remediate them.

- Make the same measurement data serve both audiences: evidence an auditor will accept, and signal the company can act on.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Execution

- Establish productive working relationships with GRC (SAC, SAF, Governance, Risk Management, TPRM), Enterprise Security, Product Security, Security Operations, IT, Legal, and Engineering leadership — the teams who own the controls, the evidence, and the remediation.

- Partner with Enterprise Security and Product Security so control measurement reflects how systems are actually built and configured, and feed coverage gaps back to the teams who own those controls.

- Partner with SAC and SAF to ensure monitoring output meets auditor and 3PAO evidence standards, and with Governance to keep control monitoring aligned to policy as standards evolve.

- Coordinate with Risk Management and Security Operations on metric definitions and reporting boundaries so the organization gets one coherent picture of control health rather than three overlapping ones.

- Coordinate execution across teams to unblock cross-cutting initiatives: telemetry gaps in Engineering-owned systems, GRC platform migrations, and multi-quarter automation programs.

- Make effective priority and resourcing decisions within the team; be accountable for defining and achieving the team's OKRs and KPIs.

Technology Decisions

- Lead build-vs.-buy evaluations for CSPM, SSPM, GRC automation, and security posture tooling; assess platforms on integration capability, measurement fidelity, maintenance cost, and fit with existing pipelines, and make the recommendation to Security and GRC leadership.

- Keep the program's operating costs defensible — cloud spend, tooling, and the engineering time monitoring consumes — and be able to explain the tradeoff between monitoring coverage and what it costs to run at scale.

- Track what the program will need to measure next — changes in Databricks' architecture and threat exposure, new SOC 2 criteria, FedRAMP continuous monitoring changes, and AI governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act) — and translate them into roadmap decisions early enough to build for them.

What We Look For

- 2+ years of prior management experience leading Engineering or Security engineering teams.

- Typically 12+ years of experience, or an advanced degree plus 8 years, preferably focused on security engineering, security posture monitoring, or compliance automation.

- Sufficient technical depth to review the work of the team: can read and critique Python automation, evaluate an integration architecture, and assess whether a monitoring approach will hold up in production.

- Solid understanding of security controls and where they fail in practice — identity and access, configuration management, logging coverage, vulnerability management, and data protection — enough to judge whether a given measurement is telling you anything useful.

- Solid cloud security knowledge across at least one major platform (AWS, Azure, GCP) — IAM, audit logging, CSPM concepts, and cloud-native security services.

- Working knowledge of compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, or equivalent) at a level sufficient to assess whether a control monitoring design will satisfy an auditor.

- Previous experience building security posture monitoring or compliance automation at scale, with attention to accuracy, coverage, and cost tradeoffs (experience with Databricks is preferred).

- Focused on defining and driving efficiencies and improvements within the team; accountable for defining and achieving targets (e.g. OKRs, KPIs).

- Makes effective priority decisions on resourcing and alignment within the team.

- Strong communicator across technical, GRC, and executive audiences — can explain automation architecture to auditors and compliance requirements to engineers.

Nice to Have

- Experience with cloud security posture management (CSPM/SSPM) platforms at an architecture level.

- Experience with FedRAMP continuous monitoring programs at a leadership level.

- Hands-on background with GRC automation platforms (Vanta, Drata, ServiceNow GRC, Archer, or equivalent) at an implementation or architecture level.

- Experience building automated monitoring for AI system controls and AI governance frameworks.

- Track record of building or scaling a security measurement or compliance engineering function from early-stage to mature operations.

- Background in security operations, detection engineering, or security architecture that informs which controls are worth measuring.

- Experience with front-end development.

- CISSP, CISM, CISA, or equivalent certifications.

At Databricks, we are passionate about empowering data teams to tackle the world’s most challenging problems — from bringing the next mode of transportation to reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We achieve this by building and operating the world’s best data and AI infrastructure platform, enabling our customers to leverage deep data insights and enhance their business. Founded by engineers — and customer-obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to tackle technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started. 

We are seeking an experienced Tech Lead to shape the future of platform observability and proactive monitoring. This is a high-impact technical role for someone who thrives at the intersection of platform reliability, incident response, and customer obsession.You will serve as a critical first responder for the Databricks Platform, leading complex investigations, designing observability solutions, and driving systemic improvements that enhance customer experience and platform stability.

The successful candidate will be responsible for developing monitoring solutions, alerting mechanisms, and customer-focused incident detection tools. They will also work closely with cross-functional engineering teams to investigate and resolve incidents, perform root cause analyses, and propose solutions to improve the reliability and stability of the Databricks Platform.

The impact you will have: 

- 

Lead platform incident investigation, coordinating cross-functional teams through rapid detection, mitigation, and resolution to minimize customer impact.

- 

Conduct thorough post-incident root cause analysis across infrastructure, services, and cloud providers to identify systemic patterns and prevent future occurrences.

- 

Design and implement customer-focused alerting pipelines and end-to-end observability workflows to enhance detection coverage and reduce mean time to detection.

Minimum of 6 years of experience as an SRE, DevOps Engineer, Production Engineer, or similar role.

Production-level experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP) and proficiency in container and orchestration technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

- 

Hands-on experience with monitoring, logging, and alerting tools such as ELK, Prometheus, Grafana, PagerDuty, etc. Ability to architect monitoring solutions that correlate metrics, logs, and traces.

- 

Strong proficiency in Python or similar languages with the ability to build production-quality automation tools.

- 

Experience owning critical phases of the incident lifecycle from detection through resolution and post-mortem analysis in demanding production environments.

- 

BS or Master's, or PhD in Computer Science or Computer Engineering, or related Engineering field.

postings.location: Amsterdam, Netherlands; Berlin, Germany; London, United Kingdom
postings.description:
P-1626

Senior Product Designer

At Databricks, we design tools that make complex data and AI workflows intuitive and powerful. Our mission is to simplify how data is connected, understood, and activated so organizations can turn information into business outcomes. Designers at Databricks combine strong visual craft with systems thinking. They shape products used by some of the most advanced data teams in the world, and increasingly by the business users and AI agents working alongside them.

We're hiring Product Designers to join our design team and own design for an area of the Databricks Platform. Teams span the platform, from data engineering and analytics to databases, apps, and AI agents. We match each designer to the area where their skills and interests will have the most impact. You'll design for both technical and business users of data, making powerful capabilities feel clear, controllable, and trustworthy for enterprise customers.

The impact you will have

- Own your area end to end. Sharpen the problem, set the design direction, and carry the work from framing and interaction models through visual polish and shipped detail.

- Set the quality bar. Make the critical design decisions in your area, review work from designers, PM, engineering, and AI tools, and have the hands-on skill to improve it yourself.

- Advocate with evidence. Stay in regular contact with customers, choose research methods that fit the decision, and turn research into insights others can act on.

- Show the experience got better. Define what success looks like for the key tasks users need to get done, and show the improvement through usability testing, research, and how people actually use what shipped.

- Influence through the work. Move product and engineering decisions with prototypes, keep design reviews focused, and communicate clearly in writing and in person.

- Prototype to explore and align. Use interactive prototypes as a primary thinking tool to explore ambiguous problems, reduce risk, and align the team on a direction.

- Design directly in the codebase with coding agents. Use AI coding agents to ship well-scoped design changes alongside engineers, rather than handing off static mocks.

- Define reusable UX principles. Create interaction patterns and frameworks other teams reuse, and drive consistency through a strong, cross-platform design system.

- Raise the level of critique. Give and invite high-quality feedback, and help make clear decisions together with product and engineering.

What we look for

- 5+ years of product design work experience.

- A bachelor's or master's degree in design, computer science, human-computer interaction, or a related field.

- A portfolio demonstrating your end-to-end design process, from inception to production.

- Demonstrated ability to lead large and complex design projects and balance the needs of diverse stakeholders.

- A systems thinker who has the vision to design the big picture, and the tactical ability to break it down so that engineering can succeed in building it incrementally.

- A deep understanding of business goals, customer needs, emerging AI capabilities, and the evolving data and technology landscape.

- Self-directed and comfortable in ambiguity. You help shape product direction when the path isn't defined.

- Beautiful visual and interaction work rooted in a data-driven, well-researched UX process.

Nice to have

- Experience designing developer tools, data/analytics products, AI/ML products, or enterprise software.

- Experience designing products that bridge the gap between technical and business users.

- The strongest candidates have demonstrated experience using modern development and AI-assisted coding tools to prototype ideas, understand implementation tradeoffs, and collaborate deeply with engineering teams.

postings.title: Sr Production Engineer- Public Sector
postings.description:
P-1602

About Databricks

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

The Role

At Databricks, we don’t just use the cloud; we are "cloud maximalists." Unlike most companies that treat multi-cloud as a backup strategy, we run our platform across every region of every major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, and GCP) simultaneously. This creates a massive, high-consequence engineering surface area that requires a unique breed of Production Engineer.

In this role, you won’t just run our cloud environments; you will own and evolve the secure infrastructure, access patterns, and guardrails that keep Databricks’ global platform safe and compliant in production. You will be responsible for the "sovereign layer" of our infrastructure, ensuring that our Data Intelligence Platform operates with 100% reliability and security in highly regulated, air-gapped, and sovereign environments. If you are an engineer who views infrastructure as a software problem and thrives on the complexity of global-scale networking, IAM, and automation, this is your team.

The Impact You’ll Have

Security-Focused Cloud Operations

- Design, automate, and operate the IAM, account/subscription, and project lifecycle across AWS, Azure, and GCP, enforcing least-privilege and standardized access patterns at scale.

- Review, implement, and continuously improve cloud identity and access policies (IAM, Okta, Opal) to align with Databricks security standards and audit requirements.

Production Engineering & Automation

- Build and maintain reliable, observable automation and tooling to apply cloud changes (roles, policies, accounts, networking) safely and repeatedly.

- Treat operational and security issues as software problems: eliminate toil, drive root-cause analysis, and codify fixes into infrastructure and tooling.

Security Data Pipelines & Compliance

- Own and improve security and audit logging data pipelines from cloud providers into our internal systems, ensuring timely, accurate data for detection, investigations, and audits.

- Partner with Security, Compliance, and Audit teams to provide evidence, clarifications, and policy updates that keep our environments aligned with evolving standards.

Regulated & Specialized Environments

- Operate and improve specialized, highly regulated environments (e.g., FedRAMP / GovCloud) including release management, patching cadences, and supporting secure access workflows (e.g., SAW).

- Ensure high availability and resiliency for critical security and access infrastructure across these environments.

On-Call & Incident Response

- Participate in a 24x7 on-call rotation for high-severity incidents impacting cloud accounts, IAM, or security data pipelines.

- Act as a key partner to product engineering, security engineering, and field teams during incidents to restore service and harden systems for the future.

What We Look For

- Required: Candidates have active Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance.

- Nice to have: Possession of a current polygraph (Counterintelligence or Full Scope) is highly desired and considered a significant plus.

- Education- BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in production engineering, SRE, security engineering, or cloud infrastructure roles.

- Cloud & Infrastructure Expertise

- Deep hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) in areas such as IAM, networking, accounts/subscriptions/projects, and audit logging.

- Strong background in Infrastructure-as-Code and automation (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, or similar) and CI/CD for infrastructure changes.

- Security & Compliance Mindset

- Proven experience working in or with security-sensitive or regulated environments (e.g., SOC2, FedRAMP, ISO 27001, financial services, public sector) and translating requirements into concrete technical controls.

- Familiarity with access review processes, policy baselines, and audit evidence for cloud environment.

- Operational Excellence

- Demonstrated success running high-availability, security-critical services, including on-call responsibilities and incident management.

- Strong debugging and problem-solving skills across distributed systems, with the ability to navigate ambiguous issues spanning multiple teams and platforms. 

Bonus

- Experience with Okta, Opal, or similar identity/access tooling.

- Background operating secure admin workstations (SAW) or comparable hardened access patterns.

- Experience migrating cloud accounts or subscriptions during M&A or large-scale reorganizations.
