Our mission at Databricks is to radically simplify the whole data lifecycle from ingestion to ETL, BI, and all the way up to ML/AI with a unified platform. - Query compilation and optimization

- Data security

- Resource management

- Transaction coordination

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high value challenges that are central to their own missions.

Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark™, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, California to a global organization with over 1000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest growing SaaS companies in the world.

Our engineering teams build highly technical products that fulfill real, important needs in the world. We constantly push the boundaries of data and AI technology, while simultaneously operating with the resilience, security and scale that is critical to making customers successful on our platform.

We develop and operate one of the largest scale software platforms. The fleet consists of millions of virtual machines, generating terabytes of logs and processing exabytes of data per day. At our scale, we regularly observe cloud hardware, network, and operating system faults, and our software must gracefully shield our customers from any of the above.

Modern data analysis employs sophisticated methods such as machine learning that go well beyond the roll-up and drill-down capabilities of traditional SQL query engines. As a software engineer on the Runtime team at Databricks, you will be building the next generation distributed data storage and processing systems that can outperform specialized SQL query engines in relational query performance, yet provide the expressiveness and programming abstractions to support diverse workloads ranging from ETL to data science.

Below are some example projects:

Apache Spark™: Develop the de facto open source standard framework for big data.

Data Plane Storage: Deliver reliable and high performance services and client libraries for storing and accessing humongous amount of data on cloud storage backends, e.g., AWS S3, Azure Blob Store.

Delta Lake: A storage management system that combines the scale and cost-efficiency of data lakes, the performance and reliability of a data warehouse, and the low latency of streaming. Its higher level abstractions and guarantees, including ACID transactions and time travel, drastically simplify the complexity of real-world data engineering architecture.

Delta Pipelines: It's difficult to manage even a single data engineering pipeline. The goal of the Delta Pipelines project is to make it simple and possible to orchestrate and operate tens of thousands of data pipelines. It provides a higher level abstraction for expressing data pipelines and enables customers to deploy, test & upgrade pipelines and eliminate operational burdens for managing and building high quality data pipelines.

Performance Engineering: Build the next generation query optimizer and execution engine that's fast, tuning free, scalable, and robust.

What we look for:

- BS in Computer Science, related technical field or equivalent practical experience.

- Optional: MS or PhD in databases, distributed systems.

- Comfortable working towards a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables.

- Driven by delivering customer value and impact.

- 8+ years of production level experience in either Java, Scala or C++.

- Strong foundation in algorithms and data structures and their real-world use cases.

- Experience with distributed systems, databases, and big data systems (Apache Spark™, Hadoop).

As a Fullstack software engineer, you will work with your team and product management to make insights from data simple. We are looking for engineers that are customer obsessed, who can take on the full scope of the product and user experience beyond the technical implementation. You'll set the foundation for how we build robust, scalable and delightful products.

Vancouver will be the newest R&D center for Databricks, expanding our presence in the Pacific Northwest. We are actively hiring world-class engineers to join us on our mission to democratize data + AI. 

We envision the Vancouver site becoming a key driver of product innovation at Databricks. To start, we’re bringing a few strategic areas to the Vancouver site and we have several open roles across the teams below, including:

- Log Analytics - Our customers increasingly use Databricks to analyze petabyte-scale logs in real time. This creates new challenges across the entire data processing pipeline, including ingestion, indexing, processing, and the user experience itself.

- AI/BI - AI/BI is redefining Business Intelligence for the AI age. From rich dashboarding and advanced visualizations to powerful talk-to-your-data solutions, the products we are building involve exciting technical challenges across the entire stack.

We recently launched our first Semantics modelling capability, Unity Catalog Metrics, this past Data + AI Summit but we have a lot more in store. Engineers on this team work at the intersection of large scale distributed systems, data modeling, governance, and AI enablement.

- Databricks Apps - Databricks Apps is one of the fastest growing products at Databricks, used by more than 2,500 customers who have created more than 20,000 apps — and it was only GA’ed this past June. The Apps team is one of the few teams that are exposed to low-level platform components (k8s, networking), owns fundamental tech (apps runtime and proxy), and is heavily investing in app builder AI agents.

As a staff software engineer for GenAI inference, you will lead the architecture, development, and optimization of the inference engine that powers Databricks Foundation Model API.. postings.title: Staff Software Engineer, Lakeflow Pipelines DR
postings.location: Mountain View, California; San Francisco, California
postings.description:
RDQ427R70

Our mission at Databricks is to radically simplify the data lifecycle with a unified Lakehouse platform for data engineering, analytics, and AI. The Lakehouse addresses major challenges in enterprise data platforms, including reliability, data staleness, operational complexity, total cost of ownership, and data lock-in. Learn more about the Lakehouse architecture.

Lakeflow is a critical part of this vision, helping customers build and operate streaming and batch ETL pipelines that power business-critical data products. As these workloads become increasingly mission-critical, customers need them to continue operating through infrastructure failures and cloud-region outages.

As a Staff Engineer on the part of the Lakeflow Disaster Recovery team, you will design and implement distributed systems that replicate and recover pipelines across regions. A pipeline is more than source code and output tables: it includes streaming checkpoints, source offsets, stateful operator state, table versions, transaction metadata, schedules, and dependencies across a dataflow graph. You will solve challenging problems involving consistency, idempotency, causal ordering, failover, failback, and safe recovery without silent data loss or duplication.

You will work in one or more of the following areas:

- Cross-region replication and recovery for Lakeflow pipelines, streaming tables, and materialized views

- Distributed consistency across pipeline dependencies, table versions, and transaction logs

- Failover and failback workflows with conservative correctness guardrails

- Deep clone, metadata reconciliation, observability, and failure-injection testing

- High-fidelity recovery simulations, game-day testing, and formal reasoning about failure modes

What we look for:

- A passion for distributed systems, databases, storage systems, streaming systems, or reliability engineering

- Strong software engineering skills in Java, Scala, C++, Go, Python, or a similar production language

- Understanding of consistency, transactions, idempotency, replication, checkpointing, and data lineage

- Ability to define and work toward a multi-year technical vision with incremental, production-quality deliverables

- 8+ years of experience working on related systems preferred

- Optional: PhD or advanced research experience in databases, distributed systems, or storage

This role offers the opportunity to build the foundations of resilient Lakehouse computing and help customers keep their data pipelines running when failure matters most.

The Role

As enterprise data enclaves and Generative AI applications become mission-critical to national security and public sector modernization, maintaining the architectural resilience and operational integrity of the underlying platform is paramount. Databricks is seeking a Staff Systems Development Engineer (GovOps) to join our Cleared Engineering team in McLean, VA. Sitting at the vital intersection of core infrastructure operations and active platform reliability, this team serves as the ultimate technical authority for our platform across GovCloud, FedRAMP High, and air-gapped environments. 

In this staff-level capacity, you will operate as a technical force multiplier, moving beyond complex escalation resolution to architect long-term system stability, drive fleet-wide supportability features, and eliminate systemic operational bottlenecks across multiple platform domains, including Compute, Networking, Storage, IAM, and OS internals. Serving as a primary technical pillar, you will bridge the gap between uncleared core engineering teams and cleared high-side environments, providing high-side technical leadership, virtual and physical escorts, and precise cross-boundary communication. If you are a seasoned systems authority who thrives under pressure, excels at designing tooling for constrained environments, and wants to shape the secure infrastructure powering next-generation federal AI workloads, this role offers unmatched scope and strategic impact. 

The Impact You’ll Have

- Architect High-Side Platform Reliability: Serve as the subject matter expert across multiple platform domains (Compute, Networking, Storage, OS), designing end-to-end operational workarounds and resolving the most complex escalations within air-gapped and GovCloud enclaves. 

- Bridge Engineering Boundaries: Act as the lead technical interface and escort between uncleared core engineering teams and secure facilities, ensuring precise, succinct relay of system states, compliance constraints, and high-side operational requirements. 

- Drive Fleet-Wide Supportability & Tooling: Identify systemic issue patterns across federal environments and author custom Python, Bash, or Go diagnostic tools, notebooks, and automated workflows to raise operational efficiency across the entire engineering organization. 

- Partner with Core Engineering: Collaborate directly with Product and Core Engineering leaders to root-cause platform defects, influence product roadmaps, and integrate long-term supportability features into the core codebase. 

- Lead Critical Incident Response: Anchor high-consequence platform incidents under intense pressure, establishing triage structure, making authoritative technical calls with incomplete data, and framing strategic communications for senior government and internal stakeholders.

- Minimum Qualifications

- Required: Candidates have active Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance.

- Nice to have: Possession of a current polygraph (Counterintelligence or Full Scope) is highly desired and considered a significant plus.

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Systems Engineering, Mathematics, or equivalent practical experience.

- 7+ years of experience in Systems Engineering, Cloud Infrastructure, Senior Support Engineering, DevSecOps, or a related technical operations role. 

- Deep expertise in Linux/Unix operating-system internals, networking, process/resource debugging, and distributed systems. 

- Hands-on proficiency in Python, Bash, Go, or Java with the ability to read source code, debug software defects, and write custom diagnostic scripts. 

- Proven experience managing, debugging, and operating cloud infrastructure across public or federal cloud boundaries (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, or GCP). 

- Solid working knowledge of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation, along with container orchestration mechanics (Docker/Kubernetes).

postings.location: Mountain View, California; San Francisco, California

SLSQ327R892

At Databricks, we are passionate about helping data teams solve the world's most challenging problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.

Databricks is looking for a motivated Strategy and Execution Manager to join our Deal Desk Transformation team that helps define Quote-to-Order (QtO) strategy and drive scalability. You will collaborate with the Deal Desk functions, senior leaders, and stakeholders across lines of business to execute on process and system enhancement projects. You will also own the operating model and automation roadmap for cloud Marketplace Private Offers across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Your ability to manage resistance to change, lead cross-functional conversations, and influence stakeholders sets you apart. You thrive in a dynamic environment and excel at problem-solving, project management, and driving results. You are passionate about helping us build a Deal Desk function with industry-leading business agility, process scalability, and automation in an environment of rapid growth.

postings.title: Strategy & Operations Manager - Demand Gen Programs (APJ)
postings.description:
SLSQ327R270

The Demand Gen Programs team works directly with Databricks' Sales Development and Sales leaders to build a world-class top-of-funnel engine. We give every xDR and AE the programs, plays and insights they need to turn market potential into predictable pipeline and revenue.

We work where strategy, AI and the field meet. We own the programs that are moving scaled, AI-native demand gen from an experiment to the way Databricks prospects by default.

We're hiring a Manager, Demand Gen programs to own demand gen programs across our APJ business. That covers markets as different as ANZ, Japan, Korea, India and ASEAN, each with its own buyers, languages and ways of selling. You'll be the APJ Sales Development organization's strategic and operational partner, and the role has three core pillars:

- Run demand gen programs end to end : Be a true business partner to Sales Development leadership. You'll design, align, prioritize, launch, report on and inspect the global and regional demand gen programs that run in APJ. You'll turn global programs into regional versions that work in each market, and you'll run day-to-day program management with real rigor: cadences, timelines, owners and follow-through.

- Agentify programs: Teach our AI demand gen platform how to prospect. You'll build agentic plays for different scenarios: defining account and contact targeting criteria, researching the messaging and content that work with APJ buyers, and curating industry- and market-specific content and use cases. You'll work with Enablement to roll these plays out to the field and make sure they're actually adopted, not just launched.

- Keep improving programs: Use data to judge whether programs are working. You'll define success metrics, separate what works from what doesn't, run A/B tests on messaging, targeting and sequence design, and make data-driven recommendations and pivots. You'll close the loop so that what we learn goes back into program design and into the agents themselves.

Alongside Sales Development leadership, you'll work with Sales Programs, Strategy & Operations, Enablement, Marketing, Industry teams and Analytics to plan and prioritize programs, curate content and drive adoption.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter with endless curiosity who works across teams to solve complex problems end to end. You're AI-fluent, operationally rigorous and opinionated about how high-volume demand gen should run. You'd rather redesign a workflow from first principles than maintain a legacy one.

This is a rare chance to define what scaled, AI-native demand gen looks like at one of the fastest-growing companies in tech, and to set the blueprint for the industry.

The impact you'll have

- Own Demand Gen Programs for all of APJ. That includes outcomes and inspection, metric design, measurement and reporting, governance, benchmarking, enablement, content strategy and change management.

- Shape the AI demand gen product roadmap. Bring field feedback and APJ needs to the product team. Feed the platform the content, criteria and plays that make it Databricks' core demand gen engine for both Sales and Sales Development.

- Drive prioritization and alignment. Run regular cadences with Sales Development and Sales Strategy leaders across APJ to gather feedback, set priorities and run programs, including SPIFs, contests, pipeline reviews and reporting reviews.

- Own reporting and inspection. Build the data foundation and the executive- and field-facing reporting that shows what works and what doesn't across sequences, tactics, personas, segments and markets. Turn that reporting into clear decisions, not just dashboards.

- Own sequence governance. Standardize, audit and manage Outreach sequences on an ongoing basis, both AI-driven and manual. Review design and effectiveness centrally, retire underperformers and scale what works.

- Be a force multiplier. Bring fresh thinking to old problems, build AI-powered toolkits and workflows that scale beyond you, and raise the technical bar for the whole team.

- Connect the pieces. Integrate demand gen programs with broader Sales, Marketing and Industry programs so the field gets one coherent motion. Own the feedback loop between the field, the programs and the platform.

What success looks like

- First 30 days: You know the APJ Sales Development org, its leaders and the current program portfolio. You've set up a regular operating cadence with regional leadership, baselined the core program metrics, and delivered at least one quick win, such as a cleaned-up sequence library or a new inspection view.

- First 90 days: You've launched agentic plays tuned to APJ markets, run structured A/B tests that produced clear learnings, and set up a trusted, single source of truth for program reporting across the region.

- First 9 months: Scaled, AI-native demand gen is the default operating model in APJ. Coverage, conversion and xDR productivity have improved measurably, and the playbooks you built are being reused in other regions.

What we look for

- AI fluency is non-negotiable. AI tools are part of how you work every day. You can show where they've multiplied your output.

- A "built something from nothing" background. Strong examples include program or GTM strategy at a hypergrowth company, owning Sales Development or demand gen programs, or consulting followed by hands-on operating experience. We want people who thrive where no playbook existed yet, and who wrote one.

- Exceptional attention to detail and instinct for data integrity. The role needs consistent, high-quality delivery: accurate exec-facing work, on-time delivery, honest status and zero-defect output. You spot discrepancies, trace them to the root cause, and won't ship a number you can't defend.

- Program ownership. You want to do the operational parts of the job, not just design them.

- A strategic view of high-volume demand gen. You have a point of view on how scaled coverage, AI pilots and programmatic engagement should work. You want to redefine the demand gen operating model, not maintain it.

- Comfort with ambiguity. The role doesn't come with a finished playbook. The right person is energized by that, not thrown by it.

- Technical depth. You're strong in SQL, comfortable with newer data and AI tools (Databricks SQL, Genie, custom agents), and learn fast. You can translate business needs into technical requirements and back again.

- A "get it done" attitude. You can set program strategy and also execute it with close attention to detail.

- Collaboration. You do well in collaborative teams.

- Regional and cross-cultural range. You've worked across APJ markets or with distributed, multicultural teams. You're comfortable working across time zones and adapting programs to local buying behavior.

- Excellent spoken and written communication. You present regularly and confidently to senior leaders from many cultures. You produce leader-ready decks, executive summaries and quantitative business cases.

- GTM tools proficiency. hands-on experience with Outreach, Salesforce or similar sales engagement and CRM tools; experience designing experiments or A/B tests; experience in data, AI or enterprise software sales.

What this role isn't

- Not a pure strategy role. If you want to think but not execute, this isn't the role for you. The operational work (cadences, reporting, governance) isn't optional. It's where much of the impact comes from.

- Not a role for maintaining the current model. We need someone who will challenge how demand gen works in the age of AI and rebuild it from first principles.

- Not a role for anyone uncomfortable with volume, ambiguity or pace. These programs touch the entire APJ Sales Development org, and the pace of work reflects that.

You will enable us to reimagine the tax function by leveraging our finance data lake to improve accuracy and efficiency of our tax processes and enable new functionality in reporting and forecasting. - Build and maintain internal tax applications (Databricks Apps, Genie Spaces, dashboards) that enable self-service for non-technical Finance stakeholders

- Build reports and dashboards for monthly, quarterly, and executive-level reporting

postings.title: Team Lead, Executive Support
postings.description:
GAQ427R219

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Manager to lead a team of high-performing Executive Assistants in Costa Rica & Serbia. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in developing each EA and building processes that enable them to effectively support executives across the company's G&A functions (Finance, Legal, People, IT, Operations & Security). This position requires an operational leader with excellent communication skills and previous experience managing a team, preferably of 10+ Executive Assistants.

Impact you will have:

- Leadership and Team Development: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of 10-15 Executive Assistants aligned to G&A Executives (Executives in Finance, Legal, People, IT, Operations & Security) to ensure high performance and professional growth, while providing direct executive support to 1 Executives.

- Stakeholder Engagement: Serve as a liaison between executives, EAs, and other departments to facilitate effective communication and collaboration.

postings.description:
Team Lead - Platform Monitoring Engineer

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Team Lead to shape the future of platform observability and proactive customer monitoring. This is a high-impact technical role for someone who thrives at the intersection of platform reliability, incident response, and customer obsession.

The successful candidate will balance technical depth with people leadership: driving monitoring solutions, alerting mechanisms, and customer-focused incident detection tools, and raising the bar of the engineers around them. You will partner closely with cross-functional engineering teams to investigate and resolve incidents, drive root cause analyses, and champion solutions that improve customer reliability and stability of the Databricks Platform.

The Impact You Will Have

Technical Leadership

- Lead platform incident investigation, coordinating cross-functional teams through rapid detection, mitigation, and resolution to minimize customer impact.

- Conduct thorough post-incident root cause analysis across infrastructure, services, and cloud providers to identify systemic patterns and prevent future occurrences.

- Guide the design and implementation of customer-focused alerting pipelines and end-to-end observability workflows that expand detection coverage and reduce mean time to detection.

- Build automation tools, establish reusable monitoring patterns, and resolve reliability gaps that directly impact customer experience.

- Participate in and help structure the on-call rotation, leading by example during high-severity incidents.

People Leadership

- Collaborate with internal customer stakeholders to design and execute the customers' reliability plan, focusing on observability and monitoring.

- Participate in growing the local team of Platform Monitoring Engineers, including hiring and onboarding.

- Act as the local point of leadership and a connection to the broader global team, aligning local execution with global goals.

What We Are Looking For:

- Minimum of 6 years of experience as an SRE, DevOps Engineer, CRE, Production Engineer, or similar role.

- 2+ years of experience leading engineers, whether as a people manager or team lead, with clear mentorship and coaching responsibilities.

- Production-level experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP) and proficiency in container and orchestration technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

- Hands-on experience with monitoring, logging, and alerting tools such as ELK, Prometheus, Grafana, PagerDuty, etc. Ability to architect monitoring solutions that correlate metrics, logs, and traces.

- Strong proficiency in Python or similar languages with the ability to build production-quality automation tools.

- Experience owning critical phases of the incident lifecycle from detection through resolution and post-mortem analysis in demanding production environments.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional partners.

postings.title: Tech Lead Manager - Lakebase
postings.description:
P-1584

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer-obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

Lakebase enables teams to deliver applications faster with an optimised database developer experience, integration with the lakehouse, and simplified operations. It provides a managed Postgres transactional layer for application state and workloads that combine operational data, analytics, and AI. You'll join as one of the founding leaders building out both the Lakebase product and our London presence.

This is a Tech Lead Manager role: a hands-on technical leader who guides a small team of around five engineers while staying deep in the engineering work. You'll spend the majority of your time hands-on — driving architecture and design, solving the hardest problems in your team's projects, aligning with partner teams on dependencies, and writing code — and the rest leading and growing the engineers around you, who will report directly to you. It's role for a strong senior engineer who wants to lead a team and take on people management without stepping away from the technical work.

The team you will lead (one of):

- Lakebase Platform Reliability (LPR) — Constantly evolve Lakebase reliability: cross-functional infrastructure, observability, SLI/SLO definition and measurement, and higher operational efficiency without humans-in-the-loop, for both internal and customer-facing systems, by building AI-powered automation and services.

- Lakebase Proxy — Build the heart of the Lakebase data path, the network edge that every customer touches. The proxy handles all client connections and transfers every byte of query traffic, serving every data protocol: Postgres, HTTP, WebSockets, and the Data API. We route and manage large volumes of concurrent connections, solving load balancing, authentication, and data access at high throughput, with a focus on performance, observability, and reliability.

- Lakebase Storage — Drive continuous delivery within a team of experts in storage technology, distributed systems, and Rust. We manage the development and rollout of storage services that host millions of customer databases across dozens of regions, partnering with peer engineering teams across Databricks to co-evolve Lakebase services with our global infrastructure, and leading operational excellence in the 24/7 operation of our system.

The impact you will have:

- Lead a small team of 5-6 engineers, owning execution and on-time, high-quality delivery.

- Stay hands-on: drive architecture and design, and write code on the hardest parts of your team's projects.

- Set and uphold high technical standards through architecture reviews, testing, and a culture of engineering excellence.

- Grow the engineers on your team with clear feedback and career development.

- Align with partner teams on dependencies and unblock cross-cutting projects across the Lakebase stack.

- Partner with engineering and product leadership to shape and deliver a long-term roadmap.

What we look for:

- 5+ years of engineering experience, including time as a tech lead or senior engineer, driving projects end-to-end.

- Strong hands-on technical depth: you still design systems and write code, and can go deep on architecture for large-scale distributed services.

- Experience with large-scale distributed services and the processes around testing, monitoring, and SLAs.

postings.title: Technical Business Development Manager, Startup & VC Ecosystem
postings.description:
RDQ427R630

This role is in-person and Bay-Area-based by design, so you can be in the room with founders and investors.

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high-value challenges central to their missions. Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark™, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, CA, to a global organization with over 11,000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small startups to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in the world and one of the top 5 most valuable private companies.

About the Role:

Databricks works with founders from the earliest days of their companies, when it is still just a team, an idea, and a lot of unproven AI. The Technical Business Development Manager for the Startup and VC Ecosystem owns the operational engine and the relationships behind that work, and the role is technical. You will run our startup program day to day, sit across from early-stage founders and talk seriously about their AI systems, produce a steady cadence of founder and investor events in San Francisco, and work hand in hand with the events teams at the venture firms whose founders we most want to reach. You will work closely with Databricks Ventures. This role is built to grow: you will start close to the program, the founders, and the events, and over time, take on more of the relationships and the strategy for how Databricks engages the startup ecosystem end-to-end.

This role asks for four things that rarely sit in one person: the discipline of an operator who tracks every applicant and commitment without dropping one, the hands of a builder who is genuinely fluent in AI and can talk to a founder as a peer, the ease of someone who earns the trust of founders and the partners at the best venture firms in the country, and the judgment to turn all of that into strategy for how Databricks wins the next generation of companies. Most strong candidates have two of these, and some have three. We are hiring for trajectory: you should already be strong in the operating and the building, and hungry to grow into relationships and strategy. This is one of the rare seats where operating, building, and relationship-building are the same job. 

The impact you will have: 

- Run the startup program: Own the day-to-day operations of the program, including applicant intake, evaluation, scoring, routing, and offer decisions, with precise tracking of every applicant, commitment, and outcome. Run it on AI automation built with Databricks AI tooling such as Omnigent, Unity Gateway, Agent Bricks, etc. Strong, hands-on proficiency with these tools is a requirement, not just knowing your way around them.

- Bring programmatic discipline: Own the trackers, the automation, the quality bar, and the follow-through so that nothing falls through the cracks.

- Be technical with founders: Hold real technical conversations with early-stage founders about their models, agents, data, and automation, and where Databricks and Neon fit. Earn their trust by being credible on the technology, not by pitching.

- Build and prototype: Build the automation and internal tooling that runs the program, and stay hands-on with the same AI tools founders use, so you can assess their technical ideas from a place of experience. This is developer relations at its most technical: close to the code and close to the builders.

- Assess and translate: Assess each founder's technical capability and the strength of their idea, and carry what you learn back to Product and to Databricks Ventures.

- Run founder and investor events: Design and run a regular calendar of founder and investor gatherings in San Francisco, including dinners, workshops, office hours, and demo-day tie-ins. Partner with the events and platform teams at leading venture firms to co-produce these gatherings, and build durable relationships with those teams that deepen over time.

- Represent Databricks in the ecosystem: Show up as a founder-first, technically credible presence at founder and investor events, and grow into being one of the faces of Databricks across the venture community.

- Grow into ownership: Work alongside Databricks Ventures on how we engage founders across the full arc of their journey, from a first look at their technology and ideas to whatever they build next, and grow into broader ownership of the startup function as you build trust and results.

What we look for: 

This is a rare combination, and we know it. We are hiring for trajectory as much as for a finished resume: the strongest candidates are already strong on the first three and eager to grow into the rest.

- Genuinely technical with AI. You build. You can prototype an automation, reason about an agent architecture, and get into the details of a founder's stack without hand-waving.

- A programmatic operator with an obsessive eye for detail. You run complex, multi-track programs without dropping a thread.

- The developer-relations instinct. You earn credibility with builders by being one, and you can explain and teach hard technical ideas clearly.

- Comfortable around early-stage founders and investors, and ready to build relationships with top venture firms, starting with their events teams and growing toward their partners.

- Experience helping design and run events that people actually want to attend.

- Comfort switching between hands-on technical work, operational execution, and strategic thinking in the same day.

- Based in San Francisco. This role requires regular in-person time with founders and investors in the Bay Area.

- Empathy for founders and a long view of their careers. You understand that a founder's first company is rarely their last.

- Nice to have: a background as a founder, an early engineer, or a forward-deployed or solutions engineer; experience in B2B SaaS, AI and data infrastructure, or developer ecosystems.

Location: USA (National Capital Region / Washington, D.C. Metro Area) - Req SLSQ128R37

The Public Sector team is responsible for aggressively growing top-line revenues and driving new business through the implementation of scalable, repeatable, structured systems and processes while embracing the operational challenges of building and scaling a high-growth business through its next stage of expansion. As Databricks establishes and scales its dedicated National Security practice, this team sits at the forefront of enabling mission-critical data, analytics, and AI capabilities across the defense and intelligence landscape. You will report to Mike Daniels – Vice President and General Manager, Public Sector. 

Mission:

Databricks is seeking a seasoned, entrepreneurial, and transformational VP, Department of War (DoW) & Intelligence Community (IC) to build, lead, and scale our dedicated National Security practice. This senior executive will serve as a key business leader within the Public Sector organization, responsible for scaling our DoW and IC sales organization, aggressively growing top-line revenues, and driving net-new mission adoption through scalable, repeatable, structured systems and processes.

The impact you will have:

- Build, lead, and scale Databricks’ dedicated National Security practice across the Department of War (DoW) and Intelligence Community (IC), driving exceptional sales and operational execution to achieve ambitious revenue goals.

- Create and execute new strategic go-to-market plans tailored to defense and intelligence mission requirements, positioning Databricks to win and displace legacy incumbents across the National Security software and AI landscape.

- Design and drive the sales methodologies, team structure, and coverage models needed to build a high-performing National Security sales organization.

- Act as a strategic thought leader and advisor to the broader Executive Team; serve as a true business leader and general manager, partnering closely with Field Engineering, Product, Security/Compliance, Deal Desk, and Public Sector leadership to support the needs of the DoW and IC environments..

- Work closely with our FDE team to ensure customer value is realized and our promised value is delivered

- Develop short- and long-term DoW and IC market strategies and forecasts through in-depth mission and budget analysis, and communicate execution progress and sales productivity to senior management.
